sources.news_title: Hiding in catering container, switching aircraft: How Trump survived Iran assassination bid in Turkey
Trump secretly switched planes via catering truck to foil Iran threat
sources.text:
How US President Donald Trump employed a clandestine 'decoy' Air Force One operation to secretly depart Turkiye following the NATO Summit.
Key Points
- Donald Trump secretly departed Turkiye after a NATO Summit using a decoy Air Force One due to a credible Iranian assassination threat.
- Trump was covertly transferred from the visible Air Force One jumbo jet to a smaller Air Force C-32A plane via an airport catering truck.
- Journalists and some White House staff were unaware of the deception, believing they were on the same plane as the President.
- The operation highlights significant security concerns held by US officials regarding Trump's presence in Turkiye, a country bordering Iran.
- White House Communications Director Steven Chueng defended the use of high-level security protocols, citing threats against the President.
US President Donald Trump secretly switched aircraft while flying from Turkiye to Britain last month after US intelligence flagged a credible threat linked to Iran amid escalating military tensions with Tehran, according to a media report.
Trump boarded the Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras in Ankara, but minutes later transferred to a smaller military plane - an Air Force C-32A - via an airport catering truck, typically used to load meals and other supplies, The Washington Post reported.
The Decoy Operation Unveiled
Trump had travelled to the NATO summit in Ankara in the Qatar-gifted Boeing 747-8 aircraft that was inducted into the presidential fleet last month, but he announced on social media that he would use the "former Air Force One" for the return journey.
Reporters on the old Air Force One were not informed that Trump had not flown with them from Turkiye to an air base in Britain, turning it into a decoy flight.
The US Secret Service had asked reporters to keep the aircraft windows shut as the legacy blue-and-white Air Force One took off from Ankara en route to Britain.
This is not the first time such a strategy was deployed for a US president's safety concerns.
In 2000, then-President Bill Clinton travelled to Pakistan from India in an unmarked Gulfstream aircraft instead of Air Force One as part of elaborate security measures for the brief stopover in Islamabad.
Threat to Trump or jet involving Iran
A credible threat to Trump involving Iran set the "deception operation" in motion, the Post reported, quoting an unnamed US official.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials flagged a specific threat of an attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some US troops at the air base in Mildenhall, in Britain, a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
The change of aircraft had raised questions about the security of the Qatar-gifted jet, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane, suggesting he re-boarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were travelling with him.
Implications of the Deception Operation
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked if there were any credible threats by Iran on Air Force One.
"Well, I have a threat all the time. I'm number one on their list before you," Trump said, adding, "But if I go, you go."
While Trump was in Turkiye, the US military conducted a series of strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
Iran has refused to back down on its demands that the US end its blockade of Iranian ports and fulfil other conditions, and only then will Tehran consider reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran shut down the Strait after Israel and the US attacked the country on February 28.
The closure of the key waterway, through which roughly one-fifth of the world's traded oil supplies passed before the war, has kept energy prices volatile.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had earlier emphasised that making the Strait of Hormuz secure requires an end to the United States' aggressive actions and unlawful interventions, including the naval blockade and other violations of US obligations.
Trump said in a social media post on Monday that he was directing his negotiators to include compensation from Iran for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts over the years.
The post came after Iran demanded compensation for the devastation caused to the country by the US and Israeli bombardment in the past five months.
The US president also claimed on Monday in an Oval Office exchange with reporters that the US has 100 per cent control of the Strait of Hormuz, but the situation remains complex.

sources.text:
Trump hid in catering cart in secret Air Force One swap to fend off Iran assassination threat
White House staffers and journalists on Air Force One were unaware of the dramatic switch and were left on board to become unwitting decoys to the threat, according to a report
President Donald Trump was secretly transported away from Turkey in an extraordinary plan triggered by an assassination threat from Iran, according to a report.
Air Force One, a catering truck and a secondary military plane were all part of an elaborate “deception operation” to safeguard the commander-in-chief when he departed last month’s Nato summit in Ankara, The Washington Post has revealed.
Several White House staffers and journalists remained on Air Force One as unwitting decoys to the threat while Trump was quietly smuggled off the plane and boarded onto a different flight, according to the Post.
The newspaper based its account on reviewed documentation, a U.S. official aware of the operation and another individual familiar with the president’s travel arrangements.
Trump had originally arrived in Turkey on a newly retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet presented as a gift from Qatar. Prior to leaving, however, he announced he would complete the first leg of his journey home on an older, baby-blue Air Force One aircraft.
At the time, the president explained that the luxury aircraft was departing Ankara early so that military personnel stationed in eastern England could view the updated Air Force One.
Trump was filmed by television crews boarding the older jumbo jet in Ankara before it set off for the Mildenhall Royal Air Force base in Suffolk.
But shortly after stepping onto the legacy Air Force One, he was transferred to a smaller Air Force C-32A plane. He was moved using a catering truck usually employed for loading inflight meals, before flying to Mildenhall in the smaller aircraft.
The White House did not directly address enquiries about the clandestine operation to transfer Trump onto a third plane or the scheme designed to make it look as though he remained aboard the baby-blue Air Force One bound for Mildenhall.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The Secret Service declined to comment while the Air Force, which operates the executive transport fleet, directed enquiries to the White House.
During Trump’s stay in Turkey, the U.S. military carried out significant strikes inside Iran following attacks on commercial shipping in the surrounding region.
Intelligence officials had previously warned of a possible attack targeting the president or his aircraft, as reported last month by The New York Times and CBS News. Those concerns prompted heightened security measures and the decision not to fly the newly gifted Qatari jet for the initial leg of Trump’s return from Ankara.
The switch raised doubts concerning the safety of the new plane, which the president later noted would undergo further security enhancements.
On Monday, Cheung insisted that the Qatari plane remained “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.”
The revelations regarding Trump’s covert transfer to a third plane highlight the severity with which U.S. security officials view potential threats against him amid conflict with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former Secret Service agent, remarked that such a tactic could indicate specific intelligence or extreme caution amid regional instability involving conflicts in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff said.
To leave the aircraft unnoticed, Trump and a small group of aides boarded the hydraulic catering vehicle, which had been raised to a door on the far side of Air Force One, according to the Post.
The traveling press corps, unaware of the manoeuvre, was asked to pull down its window blinds prior to departure.
Upon landing at Mildenhall, photographers captured Trump disembarking the primary presidential plane, indicating he had re-boarded Air Force One away from the reporters.
Connecticut Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal demanded a congressional inquiry into the matter.
“It is unprecedented and it’s surreal,” he stated on CNN Monday, describing the event as “downright scary.”
Following the short stop at the British airbase, Trump boarded the newly gifted Air Force One jet to complete his journey to Washington.
Speaking to reporters on board, Trump was asked directly whether there were credible Iranian threats against Air Force One.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” he replied.
He then told the accompanying press: “But if I go, you go.”

sources.text:
Donald Trump 'forced to hide in catering cart' after assassination threat
The US president was reportedly transported via a catering cart to a secret plane following the NATO summit in Turkey after fears of an assassination attempt by Iran
Donald Trump was 'smuggled off' Air Force One inside a catering container and secretly flown out of Turkey on a military jet following a credible assassination threat from Iran.
The covert operation was mounted within hours of the US President's departure from the NATO summit on July 8. Officials feared that whichever aircraft carried him could be targeted.
Trump had publicly said he would leave Turkey aboard an older version of Air Force One rather than the luxury Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, which he had used on the outward journey. He told reporters the change was for “old time’s sake.”
Cameras then filmed Trump boarding the familiar powder-blue presidential 747 through a door on its left side, apparently confirming he would travel to Britain before switching back to the Qatari-donated jet. But the public departure was a carefully staged deception.
Once out of sight, Trump was removed from the presidential aircraft through a catering container raised to a door on the opposite side of the plane, according to senior US officials.
He was then driven secretly across the airport and transferred to a third aircraft, identified as a C-32A - the military version of a Boeing 757 - which flew him to Britain without the travelling press corps knowing he had gone.
The older Air Force One took off carrying reporters, White House staff and officials who believed the President was on board. They had become unwitting decoys in an operation designed to disguise Trump’s whereabouts. The deception continued after the aircraft reached Britain.
Trump was quietly moved back aboard the older Air Force One before emerging in view of waiting reporters. He then walked across the tarmac to the Qatari-donated 747-8 and flew to Washington, preserving the appearance that he had travelled from Turkey on the presidential aircraft.
The ruse was drawn up after the CIA grew concerned that an Iranian threat against Trump was credible. The danger was understood to apply to any aircraft carrying him, rather than being limited to the newer Qatari jet.
It came after years of Iranian threats against Trump and heightened tensions following the war he launched against Iran. The White House had not previously disclosed that the President was somewhere other than where officials had allowed the public and journalists to believe.
Presidents are sometimes moved using decoy convoys or aircraft, particularly in war zones or severe security emergencies, but it is highly unusual for the White House press pool assigned to travel with a US leader to be left unaware that they are not on the aircraft carrying them.
Donald Mihalek, a former Secret Service agent who served on the protective details of presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama, said such measures had been used before.
“Anytime the president is in a theatre where there’s potential combat danger, the Secret Service has employed protective counter measures including the use of a decoy,” Mihalek told the New York Times.
He said protecting the President would always come before keeping the public informed.
“The agency is not the agency of public affairs,” he said. “The agency is the agency of the Secret Service. Their number one job is to keep the president safe.”
The operation also casts fresh light on comments made last month by White House communications director Steven Cheung after questions were raised about Trump’s unusual aircraft switch.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal, including distraction and misdirection, to address those threats,” he said at the time.
Officials had not then acknowledged the scale of the ruse or that journalists travelling aboard the apparent Air Force One flight had been used as part of it.

Trump Hid in an Airport Catering Cart Amid Iranian Threat: Report
President Donald Trump was secretly ferried away from Turkey last month and used a catering truck to covertly move from Air Force One to a smaller plane amid an assassination threat from Iran, The Washington Post reported on Monday.
The operation reportedly took place a night after Trump directed U.S. military strikes on Iran after failed negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war. Trump, who was in Ankara for a NATO summit and traveled to Turkey aboard a luxurious 747-8 gifted by Qatar, announced on social media that he would use the “former Air Force One” instead for “old times’ sake.”
However, after television cameras captured Trump boarding the old Air Force One ahead of its journey to the United Kingdom, the president sneaked onto a catering truck usually designated for loading in-flight meals and was shuttled to a smaller Air Force C-32A plane, according to the Post, which cited a U.S. official and corroborating material. The New York Times also reported on the catering cart operation.
Air Force One — which carried media and some White House staff members who believed they were on board the same flight as the president — served as a “decoy,” said the official. According to a media-pool report, journalists and White House staff were instructed to close their window shades aboard the legacy jet.
After landing, a media-pool report stated that Trump was seen descending the stairs from Air Force One and hopped on the Qatar-provided aircraft, where he was joined by staff and press. It is not clear how the president moved from the C-32A to the legacy plane.
According to the Post, when speaking to reporters aboard the Washington-bound jet, Trump was asked why they were directed to lower the window shades during the flight from Turkey. The president replied that it was “because you’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags that we have to deal with,” adding that he has a “threat all the time” against his life.
“But if I go, you go. Right?” he said to the journalists. “Perhaps someday you want to change professions.”
In July, The New York Times reported that the Qatari jet appeared to lack the proper security measures and harbored security vulnerabilities. ABC News reported at the time that the Secret Service urged Trump to depart Turkey on the old Air Force One instead of the gifted plane due to escalations with Iran.
“The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement to the Post. “As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats.”

This is a story about Trump’s Qatari-donated “new” Air Force One, the “old” Air Force One, and a secret third plane (identified by the Post as “an Air Force C-32A“).
It’s also a story about the way the Trump administration lies to the public and to the press, as well as how senior administration officials — up to and including Trump — might have been willing to go so far as to put the lives of others, including members of the media, at risk.
Finally, it’s a story of how the Trump administration quickly went on the offense in the aftermath of the “ruse” — subpoenaing some of the first reporters who dove into what was happening.
The Times had reported on July 8 that the use of the old Air Force One was a “security precaution” in Turkey and then reported on July 9 that the Qatari-donated jet “lacks the same defensive countermeasures“ as the old Air Force One.
The next day, the Trump administration — via the U.S. Attorney’s Office in the Southern District of New York — subpoenaed Times journalists, leading to the high-profile fight that ended with the office withdrawing the subpoenas (and others subsequently issued for phone records) at a hearing before a skeptical judge on July 23.
On Monday night, with a third plane now in the mix, the Times reported:
The extraordinary lengths that the government took to get the president out of Turkey in secret suggested that officials viewed the Iranian threat as credible. And it led the White House to purposely mislead reporters assigned to cover Mr. Trump, allowing the press to report that he was traveling on board a plane that was being used as a decoy.
The threat was not specific to the Qatari-donated jet. Instead, Mr. Trump was being targeted on whatever airplane he was traveling on, as The Times has previously reported.
If, as the Times reported, “Mr. Trump was being targeted on whatever airplane he was traveling on“ and, as it also reported, the Trump administration “purposely misle[d] reporters assigned to cover Mr. Trump, allowing the press to report that he was traveling on board a plane that was being used as a decoy,“ then it appears that the Times is reporting that it believes the Trump administration purposely misled reporters to publish information that the administration believed could make those reporters the target of an attack.
Think about the implications of this — “The Trump administration purposely misled reporters to publish information that the administration believed could make those reporters the target of an attack.” — if it is true.
If that is what happened, the subpoenas issued by then-U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton’s office in the Southern District of New York raise even more essential questions about what the Trump administration, the Justice Department, S.D.N.Y U.S.A.O., and Clayton were doing here — and why.
The pool reports and a brief press gaggle from that day, with the new reporting and context in mind, become all the more notable.
When leaving Turkey, Megan Messerly, the Politico reporter who was doing print pool duty, reported that she did not see Trump when they arrived at the airport at 8:25 p.m. local time before they departed (although there was video of Trump getting on the old Air Force One in Turkey. When they were wheels up at 8:43 p.m., Messerly noted that the press members “have been advised to keep our winder shades in the press cabin closed.”
The old Air Force One landed in the United Kingdom at 10:16 p.m. local time (two hours behind Turkey) — roughly three-and-a-half hours in the air and, Messerly noted, “no visitors to the press cabin.“
After 40 minutes passed by — during which time, per Monday’s reporting, it would appear the Trump was being transferred back to the old Air Force One from the Air Force C-32A — Trump appeared walking “down the stairs of AF1,” heading toward the new Air Force One.
The “elaborate ruse” was done.
Less than 20 minutes later, at 11:14 p.m. local time, per Messerly, the new Air Force One — with everyone on it — was wheels up back to the United States.
Shortly after takeoff, at 11:31 p.m. U.K. local time, Messerly wrote that Trump came back to the press cabin for about 15 minutes of questions. He was asked immediately about what “security concern” led them to take the old Air Force One instead of the new Air Force One from Turkey.
He insisted it was so that the new plane could fly ahead and “hundreds of people” could line up to see the new Air Force One.
“So, you’re saying there wasn’t a security threat,” the reporter replied.
“No, no, why would there be,” Trump replied.
More questions.
“Do you know why they had us close our window blinds? That was unusual,“ a reporter asked.
“No,” Trump said initially. Then, he pivoted, “Well, yeah, because you’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags that we have to deal with.“
“So, you think that Iran was possibly thinking of trying to —“
“Well, if they asked you to close your windows, probably they feel that way. They didn’t ask me to close mine, but if they did I would have done it,” Trump said. “These are sick people. I can see something like that. I didn’t know they did that, but I could see something like that.“
Then, asked if he was aware of any credible threat against Air Force One, Trump said, “I have a threat all that time. I’m number one on their list, but if I go, you go.”
When the reporter pressed again, asking if there was any specific threat that day, Trump did not answer — instead asking a different reporter if he had a question.
The new Air Force One was wheels down at Joint Base Andrews as 1:12 a.m. July 9, per Messerly.
The next day, the Trump administration, through the office then led by Clayton, would subpoena Times reporters over their reporting related to what had happened over the previous day.
Less than two weeks later, the administration would withdraw the subpoenas. But, less than a week after that, on July 28, the U.S. Senate’s Republicans would confirm Clayton as director of national intelligence.

sources.news_title: Trump hid in catering cart, left Turkey on a secret military flight amid assassination threat from Iran: Report
sources.text:
In a rare clandestine mission, US President Donald Trump left Turkiye on 8 July aboard an alternate military aircraft, after attending a NATO summit in Ankara. He was first seen boarding Air Force One, but was secretly transferred to a smaller Air Force C-32A via an airport catering truck, while the White House maintained he was on the presidential jet, which served as a decoy. The Washington Post reported the development on Monday (local time), adding that the mission was carried out amid an assassination threat from Iran. The threat emerged as hostilities between Washington and Tehran resumed last month, only weeks after the two sides had signed an interim ceasefire agreement in June. Citing sources familiar with the operation, the Post said the mission had not been previously disclosed and was unknown even to some White House officials. Journalists covering the trip also believed they were travelling on the same aircraft as Trump, unaware that he had been moved to a different plane. In Turkey's capital, Ankara, before cameras, Trump boarded Air Force One. However, minutes later, he was secretly transferred to a smaller plane, an Air Force C-32A, using an airport catering truck that is usually used to load meals and other supplies before flights. To avoid being spotted by people not involved in the operation, Trump and several aides reportedly used an airport catering truck to leave the plane. The vehicle was raised to the aircraft door using hydraulic equipment and positioned on the side opposite Air Force One's main entrance, according to a US official and other corroborating material. According to US officials, Air Force One became a "decoy", with only media personnel and some White House staff aboard the jet. Images captured by news media at the Turkish airport showed a staircase on one side of Air Force One and the catering truck on the other, with the container being elevated to the plane's level. The video showed the president arriving in a limousine, climbing the staircase and waving towards the tarmac. Minutes later, as the White House press corps boarded the jet, a man in a suit was seen entering the catering truck's cab. The container was lowered into the vehicle's bed, after which the truck drove away from Air Force One and headed towards the smaller C-32A parked nearby, as shown in the video. The truck remained out of view for about 40 seconds as the camera panned away, briefly obstructed by the C-32A's engines. However, it remained unclear how Trump moved from the C-32A to Air Force One after landing. He appeared on television and exited the jet via the external stairs at around 10:56 pm. On 8 July, the administration claimed that Trump left Turkey aboard the former Air Force One. The US president announced on social media that he would use the "former Air Force One" instead of the aircraft that had flown him to Turkey, a newer Boeing 747-8 gifted to the US by Qatar. Questions have been raised about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month, following the trip, that it would undergo additional upgrades. A similar operation was carried out in 2000, when then-President Bill Clinton flew into Pakistan aboard an unmarked executive jet while Air Force One was sent ahead as a decoy. Last month, when Iran buried its slain former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the Imam Reza shrine, months after he was assassinated on the first day of US-Israeli strikes in February, calls for Trump's killing soared. Following the warnings, Trump issued a warning against the Islamic Republic and said, "1000 Missiles are Locked and Loaded and aimed at the Islamic Republic of Iran, with thousands of more to immediately follow, should the Iranian Government act on its threat, pronounced in many corners of the Globe, to assassinate, or attempt to assassinate, the sitting President of the United States of America, in this case, ME!" He added, “Orders have already been given, and the U.S. Military is ready, willing, and able, for a one-year period of time, subject to extension, to completely decimate and destroy all areas of Iran.” Trump added that he had already left instructions for a major military response in case Tehran succeeded in assassinating him. sources.news_title: Trump Took Secret Flight out of Turkiye Amid Iran Threat: Report
Trump Used Elaborate Ruse To Fly Out Of Turkey Due To Iran Threat: WaPo
sources.text:
President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post on Monday.
The Post said the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the president as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
There have been questions about the safety of the new Qatari-gifted plane
While Trump was in Turkey, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were traveling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane — suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were traveling with him.
Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional investigation.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Trump said. He added to the traveling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”
___
AP writers Josh Boak, Aamer Madhani and Konstantin Toropin contributed reporting.

sources.news_title: Trump Smuggled Off Air Force One in Catering Cart, New Claim Says
sources.text:
President Donald Trump was reportedly whisked off Air Force One inside a catering cart last month, in what officials described as an extraordinary deception designed to counter possible Iranian assassination threats.
The commander-in-chief was returning from a NATO summit in Turkey when he was secretly removed from the aircraft and transferred to a different military plane, The New York Times reports.
Trump had flown to Turkey on a new 747-8 provided by Qatari officials, a jet the Trump administration has spent heavily to upgrade with enhanced security features.
But as the summit wrapped up, Trump announced that he would skip the newly outfitted aircraft and instead fly home on an older model, saying he was doing so for “old time’s sake.”
With cameras rolling at an airport in Ankara, Trump was then seen walking onto the older-model plane, which was scheduled to travel to a U.S. military base in the United Kingdom.
Behind the scenes, however, officials familiar with the reported operation told the Times that Trump had covertly slipped into a food cart positioned beneath the aircraft amid threats from Iranian officials.
From there, he was moved by an airport catering truck — the kind normally used to load meals and supplies onto Air Force One — to a smaller Air Force C-32A aircraft, according to the Washington Post.
Video from the tarmac obtained by the Post shows Trump waving toward cameras as he approaches the older-model plane, before a truck is seen moving toward the steps of the C-32A.
President Donald Trump was reportedly smuggled off Air Force One in a catering cart in a ruse due to the threat of an assassination from Iranian officials
A catering truck was visibly parked on the opposite side of Air Force One after Trump boarded the plane on July 8
The video shows a man in a suit entering the catering truck’s cab before a container was loaded into the bed of the vehicle, which then pulled away from Air Force One.
But the container had notably been lifted to the level of the plane for several minutes.
When the container was then lowered, a person in a suit stepped out of the truck’s cab, which remained at ground level, and ascended the stairs leading up to the nearby C-32A.
Moments later, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was seen boarding the C-32A separately using external stairs as part of an attempt to make the flight appear typical.
When journalists then boarded the plane they believed the president was on, White House staff directed them to close their window shades.
The plane carrying the journalists then took on the Air Traffic Control sign ‘Air Force One’ mid-flight, even though the designation is technically meant for any plane on which the president is onboard.
Meanwhile, the C-32A flight Trump and Hegseth were on used the call sign ‘Reach 18’ or ‘RCH18,’ according to the Washington Post. Such ‘Reach’ signs are typically used for personnel transport flights and those that haul military equipment.
Trump was seen boarding an older-model plane that was set to transport him to a United States military base in the UK as cameras rolled at an airport in Ankara
Trump was reportedly smuggled off the plane using a container connected to a catering truck
After the two planes then landed in the UK, Trump was apparently smuggled from the C-32A to the legacy Air Force One jet, from which he was seen descending external stairs.
From there, Trump embarked on the Qatari-donated plane to travel back to Washington with the White House press pool.
Onboard that aircraft, the president spoke to journalists for about 15 minutes, highlighting the threat that Iran poses.
When he was then asked why reporters were ordered to lower their window shades on the plane in Turkey, Trump said it was ‘because you’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleaze bags that we have to deal with.’
He then added that he has a ‘threat all the time’ on his life and that he is ‘number one’ on Iran’s ‘list.’
President Donald Trump spoke with reporters onboard the Qatari-donated plane on his way back to Washington DC
The report comes weeks after White House Communications Director Steven Cheung first suggested administration officials engaged in subterfuge as Trump was departing the summit.
‘As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him and we use every tool at our disposal – including distraction and misdirection – to address those threats,’ Cheung previously told The Times.
The statement suggests administration officials viewed the Iranian threat as credible, taking extreme precautions to ensure the president’s safety amid renewed military strikes on Iran.
But the threats were not directed at the Qatari-donated jet itself, Cheung noted as he denied that the plane posed a security risk.
‘The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff,’ he said in a statement to the Washington Post.
The Daily Mail has also reached out to the White House for comment.
This is a breaking news story and will be updated.

According to corroborating material reviewed by the Washington Post and the US official, while Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of cameras, he was secretly shuttled out minutes later into a smaller plane- the Air Force C-32A via an airport catering truck used typically to load meals and other supplies pre-flight.
To exit that plane without being seen, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated plane-side using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One's entrance, according to the US official and other corroborating material reviewed by the Washington Post.
Hence, the Air Force One was a "decoy" with media and some members of the White House staff aboard, as per the official.
The blue-and-white C-32A, a modified Boeing 757 used to transport American government officials, had been flown to Turkiye along with the legacy Air Force One and the former Qatari jet to support the president's visit, the US official said.

"As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," it added.
It further mentioned that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth also boarded the C-32 A separately, using external stairs in order to make the flight appear typical.
According to the Washington Post, while no flight tracker data could be found for the C-32 A, videos posted on YouTube showed the former Qatari jet landing which was followed by a C-32A hours later and the legacy Air Force One several minutes later.
It mentioned that while it was not clear how Trump moved from C-32 A to the legacy Air Force One after landing, the Washington Post said referring a media pool report that he exited the Air Force One at 10:56 PM.
Trump was in Ankara to attend the NATO Summit with world leaders in July.
The decoy has raised questions about how much information the US administration has disclosed about the operation since the President's actual location was concealed from several senior US officials and the American public.

The US official said that a credible threat to Trump involving Iran set the "deception operation" into motion.
There have been other times in the last 30 years when Air Force One served as a decoy for the president because of a serious threat or because he was flying to a dangerous location, another US official said, declining to elaborate.

Washington: U.S. President Donald Trump departed on a secret military flight from Turkey last month when the White House said he was flying aboard Air Force One, an extraordinary move prompted by an Iranian assassination threat, the Washington Post reported Monday.
Trump had taken the newly renovated Qatari-donated jet to Ankara for the NATO summit but he unexpectedly used an older Air Force One when departing the country, a move that prompted questions about the newer plane's security.
The trip to NATO was the first international travel for the new plane, whose speedy upgrades triggered questions over its cost and security, and took place as hostilities escalated with Iran, which borders Turkey.
Before departing Ankara, Trump said on Truth Social that he would use an older baby blue Air Force One plane "for old time's sake" to RAF Mildenhall in Britain while the new plane stopped at the same base so U.S. service members stationed there could tour the aircraft.

After Trump boarded the old Air Force One in front of cameras in Ankara, he was secretly shuttled by an airport catering truck to a smaller plane, an Air Force C-32A, the Post reported citing a U.S. official familiar with the operation and corroborating material it reviewed.
The deception operation was triggered by a credible threat to Trump, the Post reported. A similar operation had taken place in 2000, when President Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as decoy.

On this occasion, the journalists who thought they were traveling with Trump on the older Air Force One, which was effectively used as a decoy, reported being advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post said aside from reporters, some White House staff also believed that the president was on board.
When asked later by reporters why they had to keep their shades shut during the flight, Trump said it was because they were "probably on a dangerous flight." He went onto say: “But if I go, you go. Right?"
The C-32A carrying Trump flew to Britain and arrived at around 10:20 p.m. while the older Air Force One and media, arriving minutes later, the Post reported. It was not clear, the paper said, how Trump was moved from the C-32A back to the older Air Force One.
Trump's traveling press pool reported he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10:56 p.m. UK local time.
He gave press a peace sign but didn't walk over to talk to them. He then spent some time greeting service members before walking to the new, Qatar-donated plane.
When asked for comment on the revelation of a secret flight on a third plane, the White House provided a statement from Communications Director Steve Cheung saying the Qatari-donated jet has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.
"As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," Cheung said. It was the same statement provided to the Post.
The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The new plane, with red, white, dark blue and gold livery chosen by Trump, is a Boeing 747 gifted to the United States by Qatar last year and refitted by defense contractor L3Harris Technologies. It was intended to serve as a temporary placement while Boeing (BA.N) struggled to deliver long-delayed next-generation Air Force One planes.

sources.news_title: Trump secreted away from Turkey in catering truck ruse: Reports
sources.text:
Trump secreted away from Turkey in catering truck ruse: Reports
The president reportedly took a secret flight out of Turkey in response to threats from Iran. The White House managed to keep the cloak and dagger escape under wraps for a month.
President Donald Trump was secreted out of Turkey at the end of a recent international trip in an elaborate ruse involving decoy jets and a catering truck − all in an effort to avoid an Iranian assassination plot, the Washington Post and New York Times reported.
In early July, Trump had flown to Turkey to attend a NATO summit aboard the new Qatari-gifted Air Force One. But once in Turkey, hostilities resumed with Iran and Trump announced that the new jet would depart for the United Kingdom and he would fly out on the older, powder-blue Air Force One.
But according to new reporting by The Washington Post, the president was not on board when it departed. Instead, Trump was secretly transported off Air Force One and transferred to another military jet to fly from Turkey to the United Kingdom.
The method used to conceal the president was a catering truck typically used on the tarmac to deliver food and beverages to airplanes, the Washington Post reported.Members of the White House staff and press flew aboard Air Force One unaware that Trump had taken a separate plane for his safety, the Washington Post reported, citing a review of materials, an unnamed U.S. official and another person familiar with the president's travel. The New York Times also reported the story later on the evening of Aug. 10.
"We are wheels up from Ankara as of 8:43 p.m.," a White House pool reporter shared from aboard the powder blue Air Force One at the time. "We have been advised to keep our window shades in the press cabin closed. See you on the other side."
USA TODAY has reached out to the White House for comment on the ruse to leave Ankara.
Why did Trump take the secret plane?
The president’s ruse to leave Turkey came at a point where the war with Iran was escalating.
Trump, on July 8 at the NATO summit in Turkey, said he considered the U.S. ceasefire with Iran to be "over" and warned of powerful strikes on Iran to come. His comments came amid a renewed U.S. bombing campaign of the Islamic Republic.
In leaving the Middle East, Trump took new precautions to make it back to the United States, though the full extent of those precautions was not previously known.
Asked about Trump’s claimed move to ride aboard the baby blue former Air Force One jet, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung noted threats against the president.
"As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal ‒ including distraction and misdirection ‒ to address those threats," Cheung said.
What plane did Trump supposedly take?
Trump claimed to take the old Boeing 747-200 Air Force One for the first leg of his return journey to the United States.
After arriving at the Royal Air Force Mildenhall U.S. Air Force Base in Suffolk, England, it was believed Trump and crew switched back to the new red, white and blue plane, a Boeing 747-B, which they flew across the Atlantic before landing at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington early on July 9.
According to the new reports, however, Trump made the journey to England aboard a smaller Air Force C-32A. The jet had been part of the White House entourage to England and was used to fly Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth. The Trump cabinet official boarded the plane by a typical stairway outside the plane, the Post reported.
Contributing: Swapna Venugopal Ramaswamy and Joey Garrison.

sources.news_title: Trump used elaborate ruse to leave Turkey after NATO summit because of Iran threat, report says
sources.text:
President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican President was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post.
The Post said Monday the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the President as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the President’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The President at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane – an Air Force C-32A – via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
There have been questions about safety of new Qatari-gifted plane
While Trump was in Turkey, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the President or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were travelling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane – suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were travelling with him.
Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional briefing on what happened.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Trump said. He added to the travelling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”

Trump hid in a catering container to escape threats at Turkey summit
sources.text:
This will probably launch a thousand memes. But remember, you heard it here first.
From the New York Times’ Maggie Haberman and Eric Schmitt:
Top White House and administration officials engaged in an elaborate ruse to spirit President Trump out of Turkey during the NATO summit there last month, transporting him in a catering cart to a military jet because of a credible threat against him and Air Force One from Iran, a senior U.S. official said Monday.
The container in question was rather large. It’s not clear whether this was an accommodation to its occupant or not.
Mr. Trump had traveled to Turkey aboard a 747-8 donated by Qatar, which is far more luxurious than the older Boeing jets used for Air Force One, and which the U.S. government worked quickly to retrofit for presidential travel. Mr. Trump announced he would not take that plane, and instead would fly one of the older planes out of Turkey, for “old time’s sake.”
The Qatari jet traveled ahead of the older plane to a U.S. military base in the United Kingdom. Mr. Trump boarded the older plane as cameras rolled at the airport in Ankara.
But instead of flying out aboard that older, powder-blue-painted jet, Mr. Trump was taken by a food cart that had been fitted to the belly of the plane. He was then taken by car to a third plane, which he traveled aboard in secret to the United Kingdom, the official with knowledge of the matter said.
This is also interesting, from the same report:
Reporters on the older plane were not told that Mr. Trump had not flown with them from Turkey to an air base in Britain, making them unwitting participants in the ruse and leaving them, along with some White House staff members, to serve as unknowing decoys.
Imagine if Biden or Obama…oh, never mind. You know the rest.

sources.news_title: Trump's reported plane switch amid Iran threat is "downright scary," Democrat says
sources.text:
A report from The Washington Post that President Donald Trump secretly switched aircraft while leaving Turkey last month has raised new questions about the security threats facing the president amid escalating tensions with Iran.
According to the Post, Trump appeared to depart Ankara aboard the older Air Force One but was actually moved discreetly to a smaller Air Force C-32A in a catering truck. The larger aircraft then continued to Britain, effectively serving as a decoy while Trump traveled separately, the Post reports, citing a U.S. official familiar with the operation and a separate person with knowledge of the president’s travel.
The unusual reported security operation came after Trump traveled to Turkey aboard the newer aircraft donated by Qatar for the NATO Summit. The decision to use a different plane for the return trip reportedly reflected security concerns, particularly as Iran borders Turkey and tensions between Washington and Tehran had intensified.
Appearing on CNN with Kaitlan Collins, Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal reacted strongly to the report, describing the circumstances surrounding the purported plane switch as “downright scary.” He called it "unprecedented" and "surreal" while adding that the war in Iran has made the president, U.S. troops, Persian Gulf allies and the world less safe.
"We need to know more probably about this threat," Blumenthal added. When asked by Collins if he wants a congressional briefing about the president reportedly switching planes, he said, "There has to be a congressional briefing, because it involves not just the safety of the president. I want to know what precautions were taken to make sure that all of the passengers on that Air Force One, which was judged too dangerous for the president to fly on, what precautions were taken to keep the staff and reporters on that plane safe."
Newsweek reached out to the White House via email on Monday night or comment.
What To Know
Blumenthal's comments underscore the broader concern in Washington that the public may not have been aware of just how serious the security assessment could have been. The report that the president’s travel arrangements were concealed adds another layer of likely concern as lawmakers consider what intelligence or threats may have prompted the extraordinary precautions.
According to a pool report, journalists traveling with the president aboard the older Air Force One were also asked to close their window shades, the Post says.
The reported episode also renews questions about the security of the newer Air Force One aircraft. The White House has maintained that the newer aircraft has extensive security protections, but the decision to move Trump to another plane suggests that presidential security officials were taking no chances amid the reported threat.
David Axelrod, former adviser to ex-President Barack Obama, told Collins on Monday night in part that it is "stunning" to think about the people used sort of as "a decoy" and "not told that the president wasn't on board and that the deception was continued even after he safely returned to Washington." Axelrod said it is hard for him to understand.
Scott Jennings, former adviser to ex-President George W. Bush, said to Collins that this is "highly unusual," but said "it sounds to me like the threat was unusual."
For lawmakers such as Blumenthal, the key issue now is understanding what happened behind the scenes and why the reported threat was considered serious enough to warrant such an unusual operation. A reported presidential aircraft switch conducted in secret, with another plane continuing publicly as a potential decoy, seems to highlight the extraordinary security challenges facing the president during a period of heightened conflict with Iran. It also leaves Congress with questions about what intelligence officials knew, when they knew it and whether additional briefings are necessary.
DOD Revoked Former Air Force Secretary's Eligibility for Access to Classified Information
The Department of Defense (DOD) announced that former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall’s eligibility for access to classified information had been revoked, along with his ability to hold any sensitive position, due to an alleged unauthorized disclosure of information regarding Air Force One to a media outlet.
The announcement, shared by Chief Pentagon Spokesperson Sean Parnell last week in a post to X, said: "Safeguarding classified information is a non-negotiable duty. Those who violate that trust forfeit the privilege of access and any role requiring it."
Kendall told CNN on Monday that he was "mystified" trying to think of anything he ever shared that was classified. He added that he has been critical of the current administration and that he is not one of the leakers, adding that "I don't know anything about that airplane."
"I'm mystified about why they did this," Kendall said in part. He added that he plans to sue and that he found out this happened to him in the X post.
Kendall was also asked about the Post's report about Trump switching planes and he said he did not want to get anywhere near that, particularly under the current circumstances.
Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Edward T. Cummins.

sources.news_title: Donald Trump 'smuggled away in catering van' to escape assassination threat on Air Force One
sources.text:
Donald Trump 'smuggled away in catering van' to escape assassination threat on Air Force One
The President escaped an 'Iranian threat' through an ingenious bait-and-switch plot
Bombshell new details of Donald Trump's extraordinary getaway from an alleged Iranian threat on his life have been revealed for the very first time.
For more than a month, it has widely been believed the President had rushed to Britain aboard the old Air Force One presidential plane amid the threat.
Mr Trump said he was using the recognisable older blue jet for "old time's sake" to fly from a Nato summit in Turkey to RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk.
But it has now emerged the President was smuggled away in a catering vehicle onto a waiting third plane.
Mr Trump made a show of boarding Air Force One in Ankara for the world's cameras to see.
He then told everyone on board to lower their window shutters.
Then, he was secretly shuttled onto a nearby Air Force C-32A, an American official revealed to The Washington Post last night.
Air Force One was effectively turned into a "decoy" for any kind of Iranian attack - with the media and White House staff aboard.
When pressed on the flight change in Turkey, Mr Trump dodged questions but told reporters he was "number one on the kill list for Iran".
The President was smuggled off the 'old' Air Force One in a catering vehicle (pictured) onto a waiting third plane
|GETTY
The bait-and-switch meant Mr Trump's real location was hidden from the public - and some senior US officials - for hours.
Even when George W Bush was rushed away from a school on 9/11, he was officially taken to an "undisclosed location".
But regarding last month, the White House still insists Mr Trump was somewhere he was not.
The US official admitted a credible threat to the President involving Iran set the "deception operation" in motion.
It reveals how strongly US security officials felt about his safety leaving Turkey amid refreshed hostilities with Iran.
DONALD TRUMP - READ MORE:
The bait-and-switch meant Mr Trump's real location was hidden from the public - and some senior US officials - for hours
|GETTY
The President instead flew on 'Air Force Two', a Boeing C-32 which usually carries the Vice President, with its flight tracking data turned off
|WIKIMEDIA COMMONS/DYLAN AGBAGNI
Turkey, a key Nato ally, shares a more than 330-mile-long border with the Islamic Republic.
Several people took part in the "deception" - though some did not even realise.
A number of reporters who thought they were travelling with Mr Trump on the old Air Force One were not told that he had changed aircraft, or made aware of the extent of the threat.
The "new" Air Force One jet gifted by Qatar left Turkey first, in the early evening.
The President then waved to cameras as he stepped onto the "old" Air Force One at sunset.
Donald Trump mysteriously got back onto the 'old' Air Force One on the tarmac in Suffolk
| GETTY
In order to leave the jet unseen, he and several aides stepped onto a container for the catering vehicle, which was elevated to plane-height at a door on the opposite side to the cameras.
A few minutes later, a man in a suit got into the catering vehicle's cab.
The container then was lowered into the bed of the vehicle, which then drove to the smaller C-32A nearby.
US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth then "officially" boarded the C-32A using normal stairs in a bid to to make that flight look typical.
He then flew with Mr Trump to the UK - with that plane's tracking data turned off, according to independent tracker Thenewarea51.
It remains unclear how the President got back on board Air Force One in Suffolk, but was seen on TV walking down its external stairs before flying safely back to the States.

sources.news_title: Catering truck and decoy jet: Secret mission to protect Trump from Iranian threat
sources.text:
A credible Iranian assassination plot aimed at US President Donald Trump prompted an unprecedented covert operation last month in which he was secretly flown out of Turkey aboard an alternate military aircraft while the White House falsely maintained he was traveling on Air Force One, The Washington Post reported on Monday.
The covert relocation - which remained completely undisclosed until now - was executed without the knowledge of embedded reporters or several White House staffers who believed they were traveling on the same aircraft as the president, according to operational documentation reviewed by The Post, a US official familiar with the mission, and another source knowledgeable about presidential travel arrangements.
Publicly, administration officials maintained that Trump departed Turkey on July 8 aboard the legacy Air Force One. Trump previously stated on social media that he would utilize the "former Air Force One" rather than the Boeing 747-8 gifted to the US by Qatar, an aircraft whose security measures faced public scrutiny and which Trump indicated would undergo further defensive enhancements.
While in Ankara, Trump walked onto the legacy Air Force One jumbo jet in full view of news cameras. Minutes later, however, he was covertly transferred to a smaller Air Force C-32A transport plane using an airport catering truck normally reserved for loading inflight meals, according to the US official and supporting records reviewed by The Post. That maneuver effectively turned the primary Air Force One into a "decoy" carrying journalists and White House personnel, the official noted.
Trump had been attending a NATO summit in Ankara with international leaders. The operation transpired the night after American forces launched renewed airstrikes against Iranian targets on Trump's orders following a collapse in talks between Washington and Tehran aimed at ending their months-long conflict.
The maneuver effectively masked Trump's true location from the public and numerous senior U.S. officials for hours. Weeks later, it remains unclear how widely the administration disclosed the security operation internally.
When presented with detailed reporting and questions, White House communications director Steven Cheung released a statement defending the Qatari-provided plane.
“The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff," Cheung stated, adding, “As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats."
A Defense Department spokesperson referred all inquiries to the White House, while a Secret Service representative did not reply to requests for comment.
Official White House accounts continued to state publicly that the president departed Turkey on the legacy blue-and-white Boeing 747 used as Air Force One prior to Trump utilizing the Qatari aircraft.
The account from The Washington Post follows a report from The New York Times last month confirming that a credible threat from Iranian proxy groups targeting Trump and his plane forced US officials to suddenly swap aircraft during his exit from Turkey.
During the plane switch, reports surfaced indicating Israeli intelligence had alerted US agencies regarding Iranian assassination plots targeting Trump. Some US officials received the Israeli intelligence cautiously, concerned it might represent an attempt to push Trump toward escalating military action against Tehran.
However, sources informed The New York Times that the specific security hazard in Turkey that forced the emergency plane switch was distinct from the intelligence shared by Israel.
During the summit, the US resumed military strikes on Iranian targets while Trump remained in Ankara, approximately 1,000 miles from Tehran. Addressing reporters regarding the aircraft change, Trump explicitly referenced Iranian efforts to target him.
“They want to take out the US leader - me," he stated, continuing, “I’m on every list. I saw this morning, I’m on every single one of their lists. And so far, I guess I’ve been a little bit lucky, but that maybe doesn’t last very long."
