Like the older model presidential plane, the C-32A was also blue-and-white and emblazoned with the words “United States of America,” according to the Washington Post.
War Secretary Pete Hegseth was on the secret flight with Trump but boarded separately, using external stairs in an attempt “to make the flight appear typical,” a US official told the outlet.
After departing Ankara, the C-32A carrying Trump landed in Mildenhall Air Force Base in the United Kingdom. The plane arrived about 9 minutes before reporters and White House staff aboard Air Force One landed at the same base.
Television cameras and media reports note Trump descended the external stairs from Air Force One about 25 minutes after the plane landed. It’s unclear how the president moved from the C-32A to the other plane.
At Mildenhall, Trump, White House staff and reporters boarded the $400 million Qatari-gifted jet that the president flew into Turkey on.
At the time, speculation swirled as to why the older Air Force One was being used to depart Turkey rather than the newer and more luxurious plane.
The White House and Trump denied that the switcheroo was related to a threat from Iran or security concerns with the new plane, which Trump is using as a temporary Air Force One while Boeing finishes work on permanent replacement planes.
Once aboard the Qatari-gifted jet, Trump went to the back of the plane and spoke with reporters for several minutes without letting on that he was not on the plane with them for the first-leg of the flight.
The secret operation was set in motion due to a “credible” Iranian threat against Trump’s life, a US official told the Washington Post. The official did not elaborate on the exact nature of the threat.
Several outlets reported last month that intelligence officials flagged a specific threat against the president, triggering the plane switch.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Israel tipped the US off about a potential Iranian assassination plot targeting Trump.
The White House on Monday night did not deny the report of Trump’s secret flight out of Turkey.
When reached for comment about the report, White House communications director Steven Cheung touted the safety of the Qatari-gifted jet.
“The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff,” Cheung said in a statement. “As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats.”
The White House also pointed to a statement from the Air Force touting the so-called “palace in the sky” plane.
“The aircraft is safe, secure and equipped with the most advanced technologies necessary to meet the requirements of the presidential mission,” read the statement. “Those requirements were carefully crafted to prioritize mission over aesthetics, leaving much of the previous head of state interior layout minimally changed.
“No risk was taken in security, safety or mission communications, but the collective team made trades on some of the less commonly used mission sets that Boeing must deliver to support the next 40 years.”

sources.news_title: Plane swap, decoy truck: How Trump secretly exited Turkey after an Iran threat
sources.text:
Trump slid into catering truck, hid in it to leave Turkey amid Iran threat
US officials moved Donald Trump out of Turkey on a smaller military jet after a credible Iranian assassination threat emerged. The covert switch was so successful that even journalists and some of the White House staff remained oblivious of his real location in the extraordinary plan executed on July 8.
US President Donald Trump's departure from Turkey after the NATO Summit on the older Air Force One jet and not the newly renovated Boeing donated by Qatar had raised eyebrows. Now, The Washington Post has reported that the 80-year-old was secretly flown out of Turkey on a military aircraft after a credible Iranian assassination threat, with the Air Force One used as a decoy.
While Trump was seen in full media view boarding Air Force One in Ankara, he was later shifted to a smaller C-32A military jet after being transported across the airport in a catering truck. The covert plane switch was designed to conceal the US President's actual location for hours, with journalists and even some White House staff remaining aboard the larger jet believing the President was travelling with them.
Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard the newly renovated Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar. The C-32A and the decoy Air Force One later arrived in the transit stop, Britain, minutes apart, with Trump appearing publicly to have travelled aboard the latter, The Post report added.
WHAT LIES BENEATH
Trump's departure from Turkey initially appeared completely routine. Television cameras captured him arriving at the airport in a limousine, walking up the stairs of the familiar blue-and-white Boeing 747 that had served as Air Force One and waving goodbye. Prior to that, the White House had said that the US President would leave Turkey aboard the former Air Force One. In fact, the 80-year-old himself had announced that he would use the older aircraft rather than the newer Boeing 747-8 that had flown him into Turkey.
The Republican had even presented the decision as a symbolic one, saying he would take the former Air Force One "for old time's sake" and giving US troops in Britain an opportunity to see the aircraft.
But that was not what happened.
According to the Post, the new Qatar-provided Air Force One had already departed Turkey earlier in the evening of July 8.
THE COVERT JET SWAP
The extraordinary plane switch involved an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies onto an aircraft before departure. After the US President and several of his aides boarded Air Force One, the truck was positioned on the opposite side of the aircraft. Its container was raised hydraulically to the level of a plane door, allowing the 80-year-old and his aides to leave without being seen by people on the other side of the aircraft.
Media footage, reviewed by The Post, showed the truck driving across the airport tarmac to a nearby C-32A, a modified Boeing 757 used to transport senior US government officials. It was briefly out of view as cameras focused elsewhere on the tarmac. A person in a suit was subsequently seen leaving the vehicle's cab and climbing the stairs onto the C-32A.
The smaller jet was sent to Turkey along with the two larger Boeing 747s as part of the presidential travel operation. The aircraft is typically meant to be used for transporting the President or Vice President, although it is more commonly associated with the Air Force Two call sign when carrying the Vice President.
A TACTIC USED BEFORE
Using one aircraft as a decoy while secretly moving a president onto another plane is unusual but not without precedent.
According to The Washington Post, the deception differed from the secrecy used after the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, when the George W Bush administration initially withheld the President's location but did not publicly claim he was somewhere he was not.
The Post reported that a similar tactic was used during President Bill Clinton's 2000 visit to Pakistan. Television cameras recorded him disembarking from a plain white jet that had followed Air Force One, revealing only afterwards that he had not travelled on the more visible presidential aircraft.
A former US official also told The Post that there have been other instances over the past three decades in which Air Force One was used as a decoy because of a serious security threat or because a President was travelling to a dangerous location.
SECURITY CONCERNS OVER QATAR'S GIFT
The scrutiny of the newer Boeing 747-8 gifted to the US by Qatar for use as Air Force One has been brewing lately. The aircraft has faced questions over its security capabilities, with The Post reporting that it lacks some of the defensive countermeasures found on the legacy Air Force One.
Trump said last month that the newer aircraft would undergo additional upgrades. The plane had only recently entered service after extensive work costing hundreds of millions of dollars.
The White House, however, defended the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft after being presented with The Post's findings. Communications Director Steven Cheung said the new Air Force One is equipped with "high-level security protocols" designed to protect the US President and his staff. He also pointed to the broader threats facing Trump and said the administration uses every available measure to protect him.

sources.news_title: Trump used elaborate ruse to fly out of Turkey following summit becaus
sources.text:
President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey , on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post .
The Post said Monday the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the president as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet . But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
While Trump was in Turkey, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were traveling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane — suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were traveling with him.
Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional briefing on what happened.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Trump said. He added to the traveling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”
___
This story has been corrected to show Blumenthal called for a congressional briefing on what happened, not a congressional investigation.
___
AP writers Josh Boak, Aamer Madhani and Konstantin Toropin contributed reporting.

sources.news_title: Trump took secret flight out of Türkiye due to Iran threat: Report
sources.text:
Trump took secret flight out of Türkiye due to Iran threat: Report
After President Donald Trump boarded the old Air Force One in front of cameras in Ankara, he was secretly shuttled by an airport catering truck to a smaller plane, the Washington Post reported.
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump took a secret military flight from Türkiye last month in an operation that involved him being moved between aircraft in a catering truck, an extraordinary deception prompted by an Iranian assassination threat, the Washington Post reported.
The White House said at the time that the president was flying aboard Air Force One from Türkiye, where he had attended a NATO summit, to Britain. But moments after Trump had boarded the plane, he left it in secret via the catering truck and boarded another aircraft for the flight to Britain, the Post said on Monday, quoting unnamed sources.
The New York Times carried a similar report, quoting unnamed US officials.
Trump had taken a newly renovated Qatari-donated jet to Ankara for the NATO summit but unexpectedly announced he would use an older Air Force One when departing the country, a move that prompted questions about the newer plane's security.
The trip to NATO was the first international travel for the new plane, whose speedy upgrades triggered questions over its cost and security, and took place as hostilities escalated with Iran, which borders Türkiye.
Before departing Ankara, Trump said on Truth Social that he would use an older baby blue Air Force One plane "for old time's sake" to RAF Mildenhall in Britain while the new plane stopped at the same base so US service members stationed there could tour the aircraft.
After Trump boarded the old Air Force One in front of cameras in Ankara, he was secretly shuttled by the airport catering truck to a smaller plane, an Air Force C-32A, the Post reported citing a US official familiar with the operation and corroborating material it reviewed.
SECRET SWITCH
The deception operation was triggered by a credible threat to Trump, the Post reported. A similar operation had taken place in 2000, when President Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as decoy.
On this occasion, the journalists who thought they were travelling with Trump on the older Air Force One, which was effectively used as a decoy, reported being advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post said aside from reporters, some White House staff also believed that the president was on board.
When asked later by reporters why they had to keep their shades shut during the flight, Trump said it was because they were "probably on a dangerous flight". He went on to say: “But if I go, you go. Right?"
The C-32A carrying Trump flew to Britain and arrived at around 10.20pm with the older Air Force One and media arriving minutes later, the Post reported. It was not clear, the paper said, how Trump was moved from the C-32A back to the older Air Force One.
Trump's travelling press pool reported he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10.56pm.
He gave the press a peace sign but didn't walk over to talk to them. He then spent some time greeting service members before walking to the new, Qatar-donated plane.
When asked for comment on the revelation of a secret flight on a third plane, the White House provided a statement from Communications Director Steve Cheung saying the Qatari-donated jet has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.
"As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," Cheung said. It was the same statement provided to the Post.
The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The new plane, with red, white, dark blue and gold livery chosen by Trump, is a Boeing 747 gifted to the United States by Qatar last year and refitted by defence contractor L3Harris Technologies. It was intended to serve as a temporary replacement while Boeing struggled to deliver long-delayed next-generation Air Force One planes.

When the president is aboard, its call sign is supposed to be "Air Force One," since the term refers not to a particular aircraft but to any US Air Force aircraft carrying the president.
On this flight, however, the generic call sign "Reach 18," or "RCH18," was used, according to a person involved in the mission and additional materials reviewed by the Washington Post.
The aviation tracking outlet Thenewarea51 identified the C-32A arriving in the UK under the same designation and reported that systems allowing the aircraft to be easily tracked while in flight had been turned off.
Meanwhile, the older aircraft carrying White House staff and journalists appeared on radar en route to the UK. Although Trump was not aboard, it used the Air Force One call sign "AF1" during the flight.
According to flight tracking data, the aircraft received from Qatar landed at RAF Mildenhall in the UK at 6:26 p.m., using the call sign "SAM 33."
Videos posted online showed that the C-32A, which according to the report was carrying Trump, landed several hours later, at around 10:20 p.m. The older Air Force One landed around nine minutes later, at approximately 10:29 p.m.
It remains unclear exactly how Trump was transferred from the C-32A back to the older aircraft after landing.
Shortly afterward, however, the president appeared in front of television cameras descending the stairs of the older Air Force One at around 10:56 p.m., creating the impression that he had arrived in the UK aboard the same aircraft he had been seen boarding in Turkey.
The White House also published a post that night stating that Trump had landed at the British base "aboard the former Air Force One," accompanied by a photograph of the aircraft.
After greeting US service members, Trump boarded the new Air Force One received from Qatar at around 11:01 p.m. for the flight back to Washington. White House staff and members of the press then transferred to the aircraft from the older plane.
White House: "We use every tool at our disposal"
The Washington Post presented the White House with details of its investigation and a series of questions.
In response, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung issued a statement defending the aircraft received from Qatar.
"The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft equipped with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff," Cheung said. "As the president recently said, there are many enemies of America who have set their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats."
A Pentagon spokesperson referred questions to the White House, while the Secret Service did not respond to a request for comment.
The White House also released a statement from the Air Force regarding the safety of the new aircraft: "The aircraft is safe, secure and equipped with the most advanced technologies necessary to meet the requirements of the presidential mission."
The statement added: "No risks were taken with security, safety or mission communications, but the joint team made tradeoffs on some of the less frequently used mission systems that Boeing must provide to support the next 40 years."
The controversy surrounding the Qatari aircraft intensified after the New York Times reported that it lacks defensive capabilities available on the older presidential aircraft.
Following the report, the Trump administration took the unusual step of issuing subpoenas to several journalists in an effort to identify confidential sources.
Administration officials said the move was part of an investigation into a national security breach, while the New York Times accused the administration of attempting to undermine transparency and intimidate journalists and sources.
The administration later withdrew the subpoena and acknowledged that mistakes had been made in its handling of the matter.
Maariv contributed to this report.

The truck lowered to ground level and drove across the tarmac to a nearby Air Force C-32A, a modified Boeing 757.

sources.news_title: Trump snuck aboard plane in catering truck to elude Iranian assassination plot
sources.text:
President Donald Trump was snuck aboard a separate military plane via a catering truck to fly back from Turkey last month in order to avoid an Iranian assassination plot, according to a report from the Washington Post.
The widely accepted narrative was previously that Trump boarded the old Air Force One to fly to the United Kingdom from Turkey rather than the Qatar-gifted jet that was to become Air Force One, which was in turn sent back for further security upgrades. A new report from the Washington Post, citing two people familiar with the matter, claimed that Trump was actually not on board either, but was instead snuck aboard an Air Force C-32A via a catering truck. The operation, meant to protect him from an Iranian threat, was carried out without the knowledge of most of those on board Air Force One, including officials and journalists, who remained oblivious.
Recommended Stories
Everyone outside of a small circle was meant to believe that Trump was taking the old Air Force One back home and, to protect the deception, was even recorded boarding it in front of reporters. Minutes later, before it took off, Trump was snuck into a catering truck, which drove to the other plane that took him to the U.K.
War Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A, a modified Boeing 757 used for transporting government officials, using its external stairs to give the appearance of normalcy, according to the report.
Reporters on board Air Force One, who believed Trump was on board, were asked to lower the blinds of their windows.
One U.S. official told the Washington Post that the deception operation wasn’t the first, and over the past 30 years, there have been several cases where the president was made to secretly board a second plane after publicly boarding the first due to serious threats. None of these operations has ever been made public.
QATARI AIR FORCE ONE FACES UNCERTAIN FUTURE WITH NO DECISION ON TRUMP PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARY DISPLAY
Having the president secretly fly in a second plane has been publicized previously, such as during former President Bill Clinton’s March 2000 trip to Islamabad, Pakistan. Clinton was filmed disembarking from a plain white jet following Air Force One, but a deception operation wasn’t mounted before.
The White House has previously disclosed that the president was in a secret location, such as after the 9/11 terrorist attacks, but has never publicly been confirmed to have accurately deceived the public as to his location. This marks the first reported instance of such a case, though the official told the outlet it wasn’t the first time.

sources.text:
President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month's NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post.
The Post said Monday the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the president as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
There have been questions about the safety of the new Qatari-gifted plane.
While Trump was in Turkey, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were traveling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.

Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional briefing on what happened.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”

sources.news_title: The world thought Trump was on Air Force One. He was reportedly in a catering truck instead
Trump secretly switched planes over Iranian assassination threat – WaPo
sources.text:
Politics
Trump secretly switched planes over Iranian assassination threat – WaPo
President Trump was secretly taken off Air Force One in an airport catering truck and flown out of Turkey aboard a smaller military aircraft because of an Iranian assassination threat, while journalists and some White House staff traveled on the decoy plane, according to a new report by The Washington Post.
The operation took place on July 8 as Trump left Ankara after attending a NATO summit. It came one night after U.S. forces resumed strikes on Iran following the initial breakdown of negotiations.
According to the exclusive report by The Washington Post, Trump initially boarded the Boeing 747 in view of television cameras. Minutes later, he and several aides stepped into an airport catering truck through a door on the opposite side of the aircraft, out of sight of those who were not involved in the operation.
The truck, which is normally used to load food and supplies, lowered Trump to the ground and transported him to an Air Force C-32A. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the smaller aircraft separately using external stairs and traveled with Trump to Britain.
The Post said the operation was set in motion by a credible threat involving Iran. Its report was based on material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the mission and another person with knowledge of Trump’s travel.
Journalists and some White House staff remained aboard the Boeing 747 without knowing Trump had switched aircraft. They were told to close their window shades while the plane was on the ground, according to a media pool report.
Trump’s aircraft traveled to Britain using the call sign “Reach 18,” or “RCH18,” while the decoy initially appeared on radar without a call sign. Despite Trump not being aboard, it began using the “AF1” call sign during the flight.
The C-32A carrying Trump arrived at RAF Mildenhall in Britain at about 10:20 p.m. local time. The decoy plane landed several minutes later, at about 10:29 p.m.
It is unclear how Trump moved between the two aircraft after landing, but he appeared before television cameras and descended from the Boeing 747 at about 10:56 p.m. He greeted U.S. service members before boarding the newer Boeing 747-8, which was gifted to the United States by Qatar, for the flight to Washington.
The White House said publicly that Trump had traveled from Turkey aboard the former Air Force One and posted a photograph of the aircraft after his arrival in Britain. The administration has continued to repeat that account.
Trump spoke to journalists for about 15 minutes during the flight to Washington. Asked why the window shades had been lowered in Turkey, he said they had been on a “dangerous flight” and added that he faces threats “all the time” and is “number one” on Iran’s list. He did not disclose the aircraft switch.
My favorite part: This Turkish catering truck nonchalantly moving from Air Force One to the other plane pic.twitter.com/KYVm4FsG4W

It Might Have Looked Like It, But That Wasn’t Air Force One
Washington Post has a long report (gift link), with film analysis, that amid the kerfuffle about Donald Trump’s flying back on his Qatari bribe after he had made things more dangerous around Turkey by starting to attack Iran, there was a further plane switch.
You may recall that this eventuated during Trump’s return from the NATO meeting held in Ankara. The Secret Service insisted that the Qatari bribe didn’t have all the capabilities needed for the President to fly home from a war zone that he had just started up. So, the story went, they brought in the old, properly equipped Boeing 747 to serve as AF1 on the way back. But, according to the Washington Post, they went further than that.
The administration has claimed that Trump departed Turkey on July 8 on the former Air Force One. Trump announced on social media that he would use the “former Air Force One” rather than the plane that flew him there, a newer Boeing 747-8 gifted to the United Statesby Qatar. The security of the Qatar-provided aircraft has been called into question, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras. He was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies preflight, according to the U.S. official and corroborating material reviewed by The Post. That made Air Force One a “decoy” with media and some White House staff aboard, the official said.
The article lays the whole thing out and works through a video that doesn’t quite show Trump getting into a catering van and the smaller plane, but it’s a pretty convincing argument.
The Secret Service must have felt that there was a serious threat to Trump to hide him to this extent and use the plane the reporters were on as a decoy. I wonder how the reporters feel about that now.
This is also a pretty big leak. The article notes that when other presidents have had to resort to something like this, they’ve been upfront about it once it was over. But of course this is Trump.
“Air Force One” is the call sign for whatever fixed-wing plane the President is on, not the name of a particular aircraft. I try to use the phrase that way, but it gets a little complicated in the Washington Post article.

sources.news_title: Trump left Turkey on secret third plane over Iran assassination threat: report
sources.text:
Trump left Turkey on secret third plane after Iran assassination threat: report
Updated ,first published
Washington: President Donald Trump secretly boarded an alternative plane using an airport food truck when departing the NATO summit in Turkey last month, according to a bombshell report that underlines the gravity that US officials assigned to assassination threats from Iran.
Mystery had surrounded Trump’s departure from Ankara after he apparently left the country on board an older Air Force One plane, with its maximum protections, instead of the newly gifted Boeing 747 from Qatar.
But The Washington Post reported on Monday (US time) that Trump was not on board either 747, and had, in fact, been secretly loaded onto a smaller Air Force jet – a Boeing C-32A – for the flight’s initial leg to the United Kingdom.
After boarding the 747 with cameras rolling, Trump and several aides stepped into a catering truck that had been hydraulically lifted to the plane’s height on the opposite side of where the media was camped out, the Post reported.
Pool reports from journalists on the older 747 confirmed that Trump was not spotted during the flight from Ankara. Reporters who remained on the flight – which still used the call sign Air Force One, indicating Trump was on board – were asked to close their blinds, which is atypical.
Trump later reunited with reporters and the rest of his aides on the second leg back to Washington, where he faced questions about why he had swapped jets from the Qatari plane to – apparently – the older 747.
He initially denied there were security concerns involving the Iranians, insisting the swap was solely to allow the new, Qatari-gifted plane to depart early and visit a US military base in Britain, so that troops could admire the jet.
But under questioning, Trump said there was always a threat on his life from Iran, and that reporters were asked to close their blinds as “you’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags that we have to deal with”.
Asked for comment on the Post’s story, White House communications director Steven Cheung did not deny the secret plane swap but defended the fit-out of the controversial Qatari jet.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” Cheung said.
Later last month, The New York Times reported that US officials determined there was a credible threat against Trump from Iranian proxy forces targeting him and Air Force One, citing multiple people briefed on the matter.
The Times reported that the new Qatari jet does not have all the features of the older plane. It is now expected to be taken out of service in the coming months for additional upgrades.
But the revelation that Trump did not even depart Turkey on the older 747 – effectively turning it into a decoy – suggests officials were deeply concerned about the possibility of an attack.
Hostilities with Iran had cooled when the president left Washington for Ankara, but resumed while he was there, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted ships in the Strait of Hormuz with missiles and drones.
Republican strategist Scott Jennings told CNN on Monday night: “You can only imagine [that] the level of threat and the level of alarm that would have been required to set up this kind of deception must have been extremely heavy.”
Decoy flights are not unprecedented for US presidents. Bill Clinton arrived in Pakistan on an unmarked white jet in the year 2000, and used a decoy aircraft. But the secrecy surrounding the Ankara operation is unusual.
After the Times revealed concerns about the adequacy of the new Qatari plane’s protections, the Department of Justice issued subpoenas to the journalists involved – a move the Committee to Protect Journalists called a violation of press freedom.
The subpoenas were later withdrawn. But Trump argued it was legitimate to demand journalists reveal their sources when national security information was at stake.
Progress on negotiations with Iran continues to be elusive. On Monday, Trump said he would now demand Iran pay reparations for “all the people they have killed and gravely wounded” over the past 50 years, including those killed in combat or by roadside bombs, and thousands of Iranian protesters killed earlier this year.
This was in response to Iran seeking compensation for the conflict of the past five months. “I have instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any, and all, future negotiations,” Trump said.

sources.news_title: DECOY OPERATION: Trump Secretly Switched Planes In Turkey Amid Iranian Threat
sources.text:
President Donald Trump was secretly moved off Air Force One and flown out of Turkey aboard a smaller military aircraft last month as part of an extraordinary deception operation triggered by a credible Iranian assassination threat, while journalists and some White House staff were deliberately left believing the president remained aboard the iconic presidential jet, The Washington Post reports.
The highly classified operation unfolded on July 8 as Trump prepared to leave Ankara following a NATO summit with world leaders. The departure came one night after U.S. forces renewed military strikes against Iran at Trump’s direction following the collapse of negotiations aimed at ending the months-long war between Washington and Tehran.
In full view of television cameras, Trump arrived at the airport in his limousine, climbed the stairs of the legacy blue-and-white Air Force One and waved before disappearing inside. What happened minutes later was concealed from virtually everyone outside the operation.
According to a U.S. official and other material reviewed by The Post, Trump and several aides exited from a door on the opposite side of the aircraft and stepped into an airport catering truck normally used to load food and supplies. The truck’s container was hydraulically lowered before the vehicle drove away from Air Force One and toward a nearby Air Force C-32A, a modified Boeing 757.
Trump was then secretly transferred onto the smaller aircraft. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs, an effort designed to make the flight appear routine, and traveled aboard the plane with Trump to Britain.
Meanwhile, members of the White House press corps and some White House staff boarded the legacy Air Force One believing Trump was traveling with them. White House personnel instructed journalists to close their window shades before departure. A U.S. official described the presidential 747 as a “decoy.”
Trump’s true location was concealed from the American public and even many senior U.S. officials for hours. The smaller aircraft carrying the president flew to Britain under the unremarkable military call sign “Reach 18,” or “RCH18,” rather than Air Force One, and systems that would have allowed the aircraft to be easily tracked publicly were switched off.
The deception extended to the aircraft carrying the press. Public flight-tracking information reviewed by The Post showed the legacy presidential jet initially appearing near Istanbul without a listed call sign before taking the “AF1” designation during the flight despite Trump not being aboard.
A U.S. official said a credible threat involving Iran triggered the operation. Concerns about Iranian plots targeting Trump and other American officials have intensified amid the war and Washington’s role in the killing of Iranian military and political leaders.
The operation came only days after Trump began using the newer Boeing 747-8 provided to the United States by Qatar. That aircraft had undergone hundreds of millions of dollars in upgrades before being fielded by the Air Force in July, but The Post reported that it does not contain some of the defensive countermeasures available on the legacy Air Force One.
The Qatari-provided aircraft departed Turkey first on July 8. Trump’s secret C-32A and the decoy Air Force One subsequently headed for Britain’s Mildenhall air base. The C-32A arrived at approximately 10:20 p.m., with the legacy Air Force One landing several minutes later at approximately 10:29 p.m.
It remains unclear precisely how Trump transferred from the C-32A back to the legacy presidential aircraft after landing in Britain. At approximately 10:56 p.m., however, Trump appeared before television cameras descending the external stairs of the legacy Air Force One, maintaining the public appearance that he had arrived aboard that aircraft.
After greeting U.S. service members, Trump boarded the newer presidential 747-8 shortly after 11 p.m. for the trip back to Washington, with the press and staff also transferring aboard.
During the return flight, Trump spoke with journalists for approximately 15 minutes. Asked why reporters had been ordered to close their window shades in Turkey, Trump replied that it was “because you’re probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleaze bags that we have to deal with.”
Trump said there is a “threat all the time” against his life and that he is “number one” on Iran’s “list.”
“But if I go, you go. Right?” Trump told the reporters. “Perhaps someday you want to change professions.”
The White House has continued publicly describing Trump as having departed Turkey aboard the legacy Air Force One. Asked by The Post about the operation, White House communications director Steven Cheung did not address the secret transfer, instead defending the security of the newer presidential aircraft. The Pentagon referred questions to the White House, while a Secret Service spokesman did not respond.

sources.news_title: Trump Secretly Switched Planes in Turkey After Iran Assassination Threat
sources.text:
President Donald Trump secretly switched aircraft in Turkey last month after U.S. intelligence officials identified a credible Iranian threat against him, using an airport catering truck to move him from the plane journalists believed was carrying him to a smaller military aircraft, according to people familiar with the operation and materials reviewed by The Washington Post.
The extraordinary security maneuver allowed Trump to leave Turkey aboard a C-32A military jet while the White House publicly maintained that he had departed on the former Air Force One.
The operation concealed Trump’s actual whereabouts for hours from the American public, members of the White House press corps and some administration officials who believed they were traveling aboard the presidential aircraft.
The deception unfolded July 8 in Ankara, where Trump had attended a NATO summit as U.S. forces continued military strikes against Iran. Intelligence officials had flagged a specific threat involving an attack on Trump or his aircraft, prompting the additional security measures, according to reporting by The Washington Post, The New York Times and CBS News.
Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 gifted to the United States by Qatar. The aircraft had recently entered service as the new Air Force One but had drawn scrutiny over whether it possessed all of the defensive capabilities of the legacy presidential aircraft.
A presidential decoy
Trump publicly boarded the older blue-and-white Air Force One in full view of television cameras, waving goodbye before entering the plane.
But he did not remain aboard.
Minutes later, Trump and several aides were secretly transferred from the aircraft to a smaller C-32A using an airport catering truck. The vehicle was positioned alongside the opposite side of the plane from where journalists and other personnel were boarding, according to a U.S. official familiar with the operation.
Video reviewed by The Post appears to show the catering truck being raised to the level of the presidential aircraft before being driven toward the nearby C-32A.
The C-32A, a modified Boeing 757 commonly used to transport senior U.S. officials, had been flown to Turkey as part of the presidential travel operation. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also boarded the aircraft separately.
The flight traveled under the call sign “Reach 18,” rather than the Air Force One designation normally associated with an aircraft carrying the president.
Meanwhile, journalists and White House personnel boarded the legacy Air Force One, which later used the “AF1” call sign despite Trump not being aboard.
White House staff instructed reporters to close the plane’s window shades as the aircraft departed Turkey.
Why Trump was moved
The security operation came amid heightened concerns about Iranian retaliation against Trump and other U.S. officials.
Those concerns have deepened since the United States killed Iranian military commander Qassem Soleimani in 2020. Iranian officials and affiliated groups have repeatedly threatened retaliation against American officials involved in the operation.
Trump’s travel through Turkey presented an additional security challenge because the NATO ally shares a border with Iran.
The newer Boeing 747-8 Trump had used to reach Turkey had also become a subject of controversy. The aircraft, provided by Qatar for use as Air Force One, entered service with the administration in July but reportedly lacks some defensive countermeasures found on the older presidential aircraft.
The Trump administration has insisted that the aircraft is secure.
White House communications director Steven Cheung said the plane has been equipped with “high-level security protocols” designed to protect the president and his staff.
The Air Force has likewise said the aircraft is safe and equipped with the technology necessary to meet the presidential mission.
An unusual breach of transparency
Presidential travel is normally accompanied by members of the White House press corps, who serve as an independent record of the president’s movements on behalf of the public.
There have been instances in which presidents’ locations were temporarily concealed for security reasons. After the Sept. 11 attacks, for example, President George W. Bush was moved to an undisclosed location while officials withheld details of his whereabouts.
But the Trump operation went further by allowing the White House to maintain a public account that was not accurate about which aircraft carried the president.
Journalists aboard the legacy Air Force One were unaware that Trump had changed planes or that a specific threat had prompted the deception.
That raises questions about the balance between presidential security and the public’s ability to independently verify the president’s movements.
The Air Force One controversy
The episode also adds another layer to an increasingly contentious debate over the new aircraft gifted by Qatar.
Trump had promoted the new plane while traveling to Turkey but later announced that he would leave the country aboard the former Air Force One “for old time’s sake.”
Instead, the newer aircraft departed Turkey first while Trump secretly transferred to the C-32A.
The legacy Air Force One later continued toward Britain with journalists and White House staff aboard. After landing, Trump appeared before cameras and descended from the older aircraft, creating the appearance that he had traveled aboard it from Turkey.
The White House subsequently posted photographs identifying the legacy aircraft as the plane Trump used to arrive in Britain.
Trump later told reporters that the security precautions were necessary because of the threats he faces.
“I have a threat all the time,” Trump said, adding that he was “number one” on Iran’s list.
Security versus public accountability
The operation underscores the extraordinary security concerns surrounding the president during the conflict with Iran. It also highlights the difficult line between protecting a president from credible threats and maintaining public transparency about presidential movements.
The use of a decoy aircraft is not unprecedented. Similar tactics have been used by previous administrations when presidents traveled through dangerous areas or faced elevated security risks.
But the scale of the deception — involving multiple aircraft, military personnel, White House staff and journalists, some of whom were unaware of the president’s location — makes the episode particularly unusual.
The administration has not publicly explained the full circumstances surrounding the operation or disclosed how widely the deception was known within the government.
The episode also comes amid heightened scrutiny of the Trump administration’s handling of information involving presidential security, including its response to reporting about vulnerabilities in the new Air Force One and its subsequent efforts to identify journalists’ confidential sources.
Ultimately, the Turkey operation illustrates the competing demands surrounding presidential security: protecting the commander in chief from credible threats while preserving the public’s ability to know where its elected president is and how the government is protecting him.

sources.news_title: Trump secretly ferried in catering truck at Ankara airport: report - Turkish Minute
sources.text:
US President Donald Trump was secretly lowered from a presidential Boeing 747 in an airport catering truck and driven to a smaller military aircraft before leaving Ankara on July 8 because of an Iranian assassination threat, The Washington Post reported Monday.
Trump had been in Turkey for a NATO summit. After boarding the Boeing 747 serving as Air Force One at Ankara airport, he entered a catering container attached to the aircraft, an unnamed US official told the Post.
The catering truck lowered the container and carried Trump across the airport to a C-32A, a military version of the Boeing 757, which flew him to Britain. Journalists and some officials were led to believe that he remained aboard the larger plane.
Air Force One is the call sign used by any US Air Force aircraft carrying the president, rather than the name of a particular plane.
Video published by the Post shows a catering vehicle lowering from the Boeing 747 minutes after Trump climbed the stairs into the aircraft. The vehicle can then be seen traveling toward the C-32A.
US media had previously reported that an Iranian threat prompted Trump not to leave Turkey aboard a Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar, which he had used for the flight to Ankara.
Trump said at the time that he would use one of the older presidential Boeing 747s so US military personnel at a British air base could tour the Qatar-donated aircraft.
Journalists traveling on the older plane were instructed to keep their window blinds closed, a precaution often used in conflict zones.
Iranian proxy forces had threatened Trump’s aircraft, several US news organizations reported.
The aircraft swap prompted questions about the defenses installed on the Qatar-donated jet. The new plane lacked some security systems carried by the older presidential aircraft, including anti-missile defenses, The New York Times reported.
Qatar’s royal family donated the Boeing 747-8 after Trump complained about the condition of the two aircraft that had served as the primary presidential planes since 1990.
The donated jet was modified for presidential use and carried Trump for the first time on July 1 during a domestic trip to North Dakota. Its flight to Turkey was its first overseas presidential trip.
The White House did not directly address the reported transfer between aircraft but defended the safety of the donated plane in a statement to Agence France-Presse.
“The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats.”
After the C-32A and the larger aircraft arrived in Britain, Trump was filmed descending from the larger plane before traveling to the Qatar-donated jet. It remains unclear how he was transferred back to the larger aircraft, the Post reported.

sources.news_title: Trump’s Hidden Turkey-to-Britain Flight Revealed After Iran Threat
sources.text:
Highlights
- Trump secretly departed Turkey on a C-32A military aircraft rather than the older Air Force One reporters believed he was aboard.
- US officials said the move followed a credible threat from Iran against the president.
- Reporters and some White House staff members were unknowingly part of the operation.
- Trump was later moved back onto the older Air Force One in Britain before boarding the Qatar-donated aircraft.
- Officials said the operation was intended to protect Trump and keep his location secret.
President Donald Trump was secretly moved from Turkey to Britain during last month’s NATO summit after US officials determined that a threat from Iran against him was credible, according to two senior US officials.
The operation relied on an elaborate deception designed to conceal Trump’s movements from reporters traveling with him. The president appeared to board an older version of Air Force One at an airport in Turkey, with cameras recording his departure and members of the press pool boarding the same aircraft.
Trump, however, did not travel with them.
Instead, officials secretly moved the president away from the aircraft through a catering container positioned on the opposite side of the plane. He was then taken to a C-32A military aircraft, a Boeing 757-based jet, which transported him secretly to Britain.
Reporters aboard the older Air Force One were not informed of the change. They believed Trump was traveling with them to a British military base, making the journalists and some White House staff members unwitting participants in the deception.
The Washington Post had previously reported that a C-32A transported Trump from Turkey to Britain. The additional details explain how officials managed to keep the flight hidden from the press pool.
Why Trump’s travel plans were concealed
Before Trump left Turkey, the White House had publicly said he would travel aboard an older version of Air Force One instead of the newer Boeing 747-8 aircraft donated by Qatar.
Trump had said the aircraft change was being made for “old time’s sake.”
The older presidential aircraft was also regarded as more secure because the Qatar-donated aircraft had not been equipped with all of the defensive systems available on the older plane.
Security concerns became more serious after US officials received information about a threat from Iran. Officials said the threat was directed at Trump regardless of which aircraft he used.
The secret operation appears to have been arranged within hours after officials concluded that the Iranian threat was credible.
A small group of senior officials participated in the operation, including Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
Trump was secretly transferred to a military jet
The unusual operation began after Trump appeared to board the older Air Force One in Turkey.
Reporters traveling with the president also boarded the aircraft, expecting to accompany him to Britain. Instead, Trump was moved through a catering container located on the opposite side of the aircraft.
He was then transferred to the C-32A military jet.
The aircraft carried Trump to Britain without the press pool knowing that he had changed planes.
The journalists remained under the impression that the president was traveling aboard the older Air Force One. Because they had not been informed of the switch, they unknowingly helped maintain the appearance that Trump was still aboard the aircraft.
Trump returned to Air Force One in Britain
After arriving in Britain, Trump was secretly transferred back onto the older Air Force One.
He later appeared on the tarmac in front of reporters and boarded the Qatar-donated aircraft for the flight back to Washington.
The sequence allowed officials to maintain the public appearance surrounding Trump’s aircraft arrangements while concealing his earlier movement aboard the C-32A.
The White House has not publicly acknowledged every detail of the operation.
However, during the NATO summit, White House communications director Steven Cheung appeared to indicate that deception could be used as part of efforts to protect the president.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal, including distraction and misdirection — to address those threats,” he said.
The White House later repeated the statement but removed the reference to “distraction and misdirection.”
What Trump said about the flight
Trump offered a different explanation during the flight back to the United States. He said he wanted troops at the British base to see the newer aircraft.
Reporters also questioned why they had been instructed to keep the window shades closed during the flight from Turkey.
Trump said he knew of no specific threat but acknowledged the continuing danger from Iran.
“I’m number one on their list, before you,” he told the reporters. “But if I go, you go.
Right?
The comments came as details emerged about the steps taken by officials to prevent information about Trump’s location from reaching the press.
Decoy aircraft have been used before
The use of a decoy aircraft is not without precedent.
Donald Mihalek, a former Secret Service agent who worked on protective details for Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama, said similar tactics had previously been used.
“Anytime the president is in a theater where there’s potential combat danger, the Secret Service has employed protective counter measures including the use of a decoy,” Mr. Mihalek said.
He added that protecting the president takes priority over public transparency.
“The agency is not the agency of public affairs,” he said. “The agency is the agency of the Secret Service. Their number one job is to keep the president safe.”
Iran threats have shaped Trump’s security
Trump has faced threats from Iran for years, particularly following his decision to order the killing of Iranian commander Maj. Gen. Qassim Suleimani during his first term.
During the 2024 presidential campaign, Trump’s advisers privately warned allies that Iran continued to seek ways to harm him. His campaign sometimes used secret flights and decoy aircraft.
The Biden administration also increased security around Trump after receiving intelligence about possible assassination plots.
Trump later survived an assassination attempt at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, in July 2024. A second attempt took place in September that year.
The continuing threats have influenced how Trump and his advisers handle interactions with the media and government agencies.
Trump operation highlights tension between security and transparency
The latest operation is particularly notable because reporters assigned to cover the president were deliberately given false information about his location.
For the White House, the decision reflected the seriousness of the threat officials believed Trump faced. For the press, the episode raises questions about how much information can be withheld from journalists responsible for tracking the president’s movements.
The administration has argued that protecting Trump comes first.
The incident also demonstrates the unusual measures officials were willing to take to keep the president’s location secret during a period of heightened tensions with Iran.

sources.news_title: Sources: Trump left a NATO summit in Turkey on July 8 on a smaller plane amid an Iranian assassination threat, leaving journalists on Air Force One as a "decoy" (Washington Post)
Trump's secret escape: How Trump vanished to evade an Iranian assassination - London Business News
sources.text:
Donald Trump’s journey from Turkey to Britain last month was not the presidential flight it appeared to be.
For the cameras, the US president boarded the familiar blue-and-white aircraft traditionally known as Air Force One.
Behind the scenes, however, American security officials were executing a carefully choreographed deception designed to conceal Trump’s whereabouts amid what officials described as a credible Iranian threat to his life.
The operation, details of which have now emerged for the first time, involved Trump being moved covertly from the presidential aircraft into a smaller US Air Force C-32A before it departed for Britain.
The old Air Force One was effectively turned into a decoy, carrying members of the media and White House personnel while the president slipped away.
The extraordinary manoeuvre illustrates the extent to which Washington regarded the threat to Trump as serious as he travelled from a Nato summit in Ankara to RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk, following renewed hostilities with Iran.
Trump had publicly suggested that his use of the older presidential aircraft was little more than nostalgia, telling reporters he was flying on it for “old time’s sake”. But when questioned about the apparent change in arrangements, he also made clear the stakes, saying he was “number one on the kill list for Iran”.
According to a US official cited by The Washington Post, Trump boarded Air Force One in full view of the world’s cameras before instructing those aboard to close the window shutters.
He was then secretly transferred to the waiting C-32A.
The method of escape was almost cinematic. Trump and several aides were moved through a catering vehicle, with a container attached to the vehicle raised to the level of a door on the side of the aircraft hidden from the cameras. The president and his entourage entered the vehicle unseen.
A few minutes later, a suited man climbed into the cab. The container was lowered, the vehicle drove away from the presidential aircraft and Trump was transferred to the smaller plane.
Pete Hegseth, the US secretary of war, subsequently boarded the C-32A by the conventional staircase, helping create the appearance of an ordinary presidential support flight.
The aircraft then departed for Britain with its tracking data switched off, according to independent aircraft tracker Thenewarea51.
The deception was sufficiently compartmentalised that some people involved did not realise its full purpose. Reporters who believed they were travelling with Trump on the old Air Force One were apparently unaware that the president had already changed aircraft.
That secrecy was central to the operation. Revealing that Trump had left the decoy aircraft could have compromised the attempt to obscure his location at a moment when US officials believed an Iranian attack was a credible possibility.
Turkey’s geography made the security calculation particularly acute. The Nato member shares a more than 330-mile border with Iran, putting the president’s movements in a region where American and Iranian forces had been operating under heightened tensions.
The operation also marked a striking escalation in the level of presidential protection. Even during the aftermath of the September 11 attacks, when George W Bush was moved rapidly from a Florida school, the White House publicly acknowledged only that the president had been taken to an “undisclosed location”.
In this case, the deception went further: the public, journalists and some senior officials were left believing Trump was aboard one aircraft when he was already travelling on another.
The newly revealed manoeuvre also sheds light on the increasingly complicated choreography surrounding presidential travel. The newer aircraft associated with Trump’s presidency had already departed Turkey earlier that evening. Trump then appeared to board the older Air Force One at sunset, reinforcing the impression that the aircraft carrying the media was the presidential flight.
The real aircraft arrived in Britain without publicly revealing its tracking position.
What remains unclear is precisely how Trump was reunited with the presidential aircraft after arriving in Suffolk. He was later filmed walking down the external stairs of Air Force One before departing Britain safely for the United States.
For an administration that has made the president’s public movements a highly visible part of its political theatre, the episode offers a revealing counterpoint.
Trump’s security team was prepared to construct an elaborate illusion around one of the most recognisable aircraft in the world — and to keep even people close to the operation uncertain about where the president actually was.
The episode is a reminder that, when the perceived threat is sufficiently serious, presidential visibility can quickly become a liability.
For several hours that night, the most important question surrounding the most closely watched traveller on earth was not where Air Force One was going.
It was whether Trump was actually on it.
