sources.news_title: Catering Truck & Decoy Jets: How Secret Service Smuggled Trump Out of Turkey Following Credible Iranian Threat
sources.text:
- Trump secretly left Turkey aboard a C-32A military jet, not the older Air Force One reporters believed he was using.
- US officials said the move followed a credible threat from Iran against the president.
- Reporters and some White House staff members were unknowingly used as part of the deception.
- Trump later rejoined the older Air Force One in Britain before switching to the Qatar-donated aircraft.
- Officials said the operation was designed to protect Trump and prevent his location from becoming known.
President Donald Trump was secretly moved out of Turkey during last month’s NATO summit after US officials determined that a threat from Iran against him was credible, according to two senior US officials.
The operation involved an unusual deception. Trump appeared to board an older version of Air Force One in full view of cameras at an airport in Turkey. Reporters traveling with the president also boarded that aircraft.
But Trump did not actually fly with them.
Instead, officials secretly moved him from the aircraft through a catering container positioned on the opposite side of the plane. He was then taken to a third aircraft, a C-32A military jet based on the Boeing 757.
The military aircraft flew Trump secretly to Britain.
Reporters on the older Air Force One were not told about the change. They believed the president was traveling with them to a British military base. That made the journalists and some White House staff members unwitting participants in the operation.
The Washington Post had previously reported that a C-32A carried Trump from Turkey to Britain. The new details explain how the administration kept that flight hidden from the press pool.
Why officials used a decoy plane
Before Trump left Turkey, the White House had publicly said he would fly aboard an older version of Air Force One rather than the newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar.
Trump said at the time that the aircraft switch was being made for “old time’s sake.”
The older aircraft was also considered more secure. The Qatar-donated plane had not been fitted with all of the defensive systems found on the older presidential aircraft.
Security concerns became more serious after U.S. officials received information about a threat from Iran. Officials said the threat was directed at Trump regardless of which aircraft he used.
After Trump arrived in Britain, he was secretly moved back onto the older Air Force One. He then walked across the tarmac in front of reporters and boarded the Qatar-donated plane for the flight back to Washington.
The operation appears to have been organized within hours after officials decided the Iranian threat was credible.
A small group of senior officials was involved, including Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
White House defended security measures
The White House has not publicly acknowledged every detail of the operation.
During the NATO summit, White House communications director Steven Cheung appeared to suggest that officials could use deception to protect the president.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal, including distraction and misdirection — to address those threats,” he said.
The White House later repeated the statement but removed the reference to “distraction and misdirection.”
The president himself offered a different explanation during the flight back to the United States. He said he wanted troops at the British base to see the newer aircraft.
Reporters also asked why they had been told to keep the window shades closed during the flight from Turkey.
Trump said he knew of no specific threat but acknowledged the continuing danger from Iran.
“I’m number one on their list, before you,” he told the reporters. “But if I go, you go.
Right?
The use of a decoy aircraft is not without precedent. Donald Mihalek, a former Secret Service agent who worked on the protective details for Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama, said such tactics have been used before.
“Anytime the president is in a theater where there’s potential combat danger, the Secret Service has employed protective counter measures including the use of a decoy,” Mr. Mihalek said.
He added that protecting the president takes priority over public transparency.
“The agency is not the agency of public affairs,” he said. “The agency is the agency of the Secret Service. Their number one job is to keep the president safe.”
Iran threats have shaped Trump’s security
Trump has faced threats from Iran for years, particularly after he ordered the killing of Iranian commander Maj. Gen. Qassim Suleimani during his first term.
During the 2024 presidential campaign, Trump’s advisers privately warned allies that Iran continued to seek ways to harm him. His campaign sometimes used secret flights and decoy aircraft.
The Biden administration also increased security around Trump after receiving intelligence about possible assassination plots. Trump later survived an assassination attempt at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, in July 2024. A second attempt occurred in September that year.
The threats have continued to influence how Trump and his advisers deal with the media and government agencies.
The latest operation is especially notable because reporters assigned to cover the president were deliberately given false information about his location.
For the White House, the decision reflects the seriousness of the threat officials believed Trump faced. For the press, it raises questions about how much information can be withheld from journalists who are expected to track the president’s movements.
The administration has argued that protecting Trump comes first. But the episode also highlights the unusual lengths officials were willing to take to keep the president’s location secret during a period of heightened tensions with Iran.

sources.news_title: Trump Hid In Catering Cart To Switch Planes In Turkey After Iran Threat
sources.text:
Washington: Facing a threat to his life, US president Donald Trump reportedly used an airport catering cart to secretly board a military aircraft in Turkey last month.
This deception operation was conducted after a credible threat to his life linked to Iran. This happened when Trump was returning from Ankara after attending a NATO summit, as reported by WION.
Trump was initially seen boarding the former Air Force One in front of television cameras before being secretly moved minutes later to a smaller US Air Force C-32A aircraft, a report by The Washington Post has claimed.
It has quoted an US official familiar with the operation as saying that the US president was transported to the smaller aircraft in an airport catering truck normally used to carry meals and other supplies to planes.
A US official also confirmed the operation to The New York Times.
Trump’s actual location was concealed from journalists and some White House staff members travelling with him, the reports said. The deception was reportedly triggered by a credible threat involving Iran, which borders Turkey.
Trump left Turkey on July 8 aboard the former Air Force One, the administration had formerly said. Trump had also announced on Truth Social that he would use the older Boeing 747 for the journey to the UK instead of the newer aircraft that had taken him to the Nato summit. The older aircraft, known for its distinctive baby-blue colour, was used as a decoy while Trump’s actual flight was the C-32A, according to the reports.
The US president’s trip to the Nato summit marked the first international journey by the new Boeing 747-8 aircraft gifted to the US by Qatar. The plane’s planned use had raised questions over security and the cost of its upgrades, particularly as tensions with Iran were escalating.
Trump has said he would take the former Air Force One to RAF Mildenhall in Britain “for old time’s sake” before departing Ankara. The Qatar-donated aircraft was also scheduled to stop at the base, allowing US service members stationed there to tour it.
Journalists who believed they were travelling with Trump aboard the older Air Force One were reportedly instructed to keep the window shades in the press cabin closed. The Washington Post said some White House staff members were also unaware that Trump was no longer on the aircraft.
When reporters later asked Trump why they had been told to keep the shades closed, he replied that they were “probably on a dangerous flight”. He then added: “But if I go, you go. Right?”

sources.news_title: Trump reportedly hid in catering container to board secret flight in Turkey amid Iran threat
sources.text:
Donald Trump departed on a secret military flight from Turkey to Britain last month when the White House said he was flying aboard Air Force One, in an extraordinary ruse – prompted by an Iranian assassination threat – that involved hiding the president in an airport catering container, according to reporting from the Washington Post and the New York Times.
The operation took place when Trump was in Ankara for a Nato summit with world leaders, according to the Post. The president reportedly boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras, and then was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies preflight, a US official told the Post.
An official also confirmed the operation to the New York Times. The Guardian has reached out to the White House and the US Department of Defense for comment.
Trump’s actual location was concealed from journalists and some White House staff. A US official told the Post that a credible threat to Trump involving Iran set the “deception operation” in motion.
The administration previously claimed that Trump left Turkey on 8 July on the former Air Force One. The president had also announced on Truth Social that he would use the “former Air Force One” rather than the plane that flew him there, a new Boeing 747-8 gifted by Qatar.
The trip to the Nato summit was the first international travel for the new plane, whose speedy upgrades triggered questions over its cost and security, and took place as hostilities escalated with Iran, which borders Turkey.
Before departing Ankara, Trump said on Truth Social that he would use an older, baby blue Air Force One plane “for old time’s sake” to RAF Mildenhall in Britain while the new plane stopped at the same base so US service members stationed there could tour the aircraft.
A similar operation took place in 2000, when Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as decoy.
On this occasion, the journalists who thought they were traveling with Trump on the older Air Force One reported being advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post said some White House staff also believed the president was on board.
When asked later by reporters why they had to keep their shades shut during the flight, Trump said it was because they were “probably on a dangerous flight”. He went onto say: “But if I go, you go. Right?”
The C-32A carrying Trump flew to Britain, arriving at about 10.20pm local time with the older Air Force One and media arriving minutes later, the Post reported.
The New York Times reported: “Mr Trump was brought by vehicle from the third plane that he had arrived on to the older Air Force One, boarded it through a different entrance and strode down the step from the upper left-side door as he would typically do, according to [a] US official.”
Trump’s traveling press pool reported he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10.56pm local time. He gave press a peace sign but didn’t walk over to talk to them. He then spent some time greeting service members before walking to the new, Qatar-donated plane.
When asked for comment on the revelation of a secret flight on a third plane, the White House provided a statement from Steve Cheung, the communications director, saying the Qatari-donated jet has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.
“As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” Cheung said. It was the same statement provided to the Post. (The Guardian/ Reuters)

Trump Secretly Flew on Plane From Turkey After Iran Assassination Threat, Report Says
- A Washington Post report revealed Trump secretly boarded a smaller military jet in Ankara after cameras captured him walking onto a different aircraft
- The covert switch was triggered by a credible Iranian assassination threat during Trump's attendance at the NATO summit in Turkey
- White House Communications Director Steve Cheung confirmed the threats against Trump but did not directly address the secret flight
PAY ATTENTION: Mark Legit.ng as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!
US President Donald Trump secretly travelled on a third, undisclosed military aircraft when departing Turkey last month, after the White House told the public he was flying on Air Force One, the Washington Post and Reuters reported on Monday, July 14.
According to Reuters, the covert move was triggered by what officials described as a credible Iranian threat against Trump's life.
The president had flown to Ankara aboard a newly renovated Boeing 747 gifted to the United States by Qatar, using the aircraft for the first time on an international trip, but the return journey took a dramatically different turn.
The deception operation in Ankara
Before leaving Turkey, Trump posted on Truth Social that he would board an older, baby blue Air Force One "for old time's sake" for the flight to RAF Mildenhall in Britain. Cameras recorded him walking up the stairs of that aircraft. What happened next was not visible to the press or, reportedly, even to some White House staff on board.
Citing a US official familiar with the operation and supporting materials it reviewed, the Post said Trump was quietly moved by an airport catering truck to a smaller Air Force C-32A. The older Air Force One, with journalists and White House staff inside, then flew to Britain as a decoy. Reporters on that flight were told to keep their window shades closed throughout the journey.
When Trump was later asked why the shades had to remain shut, he said it was because they were "probably on a dangerous flight," adding: "But if I go, you go. Right?"
The C-32A carrying Trump landed at RAF Mildenhall at roughly 10:20 p.m. UK local time, with the decoy plane touching down minutes later. Trump's press pool recorded him descending the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10:56 p.m., giving reporters a peace sign before greeting service members and then walking over to the Qatari-donated plane. It remained unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the older aircraft without being seen.
White House responds to the report
White House Communications Director Steve Cheung, in a statement also provided to the Post, confirmed that the Qatari-donated jet had been fitted with high-level security protocols. "As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," Cheung said. The Pentagon did not respond to requests for comment.
The operation mirrors a similar move carried out in 2000, when President Bill Clinton flew into Pakistan aboard an unmarked executive jet while his formal Air Force One was sent ahead as a decoy.
The Qatari-donated Boeing 747, which carries livery in red, white, dark blue and gold chosen by Trump, was refitted by defence contractor L3Harris Technologies. It was meant to serve as a temporary replacement while Boeing continued to struggle with delivering long-delayed next-generation Air Force One aircraft.

US President Donald Trump secretly switched from Air Force One to a smaller US military aircraft after leaving last month’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, in an operation reportedly prompted by an “Iranian threat,” American outlets say.
According to a report by The Washington Post on Monday, Trump initially boarded an older-model Air Force One in Ankara in view of television cameras, while journalists and some White House staff members believed he would travel aboard the aircraft to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.

Secret aircraft switch
Minutes after boarding Air Force One, however, Trump and several aides were moved to a smaller Air Force C-32A, using an airport catering truck normally used to transport meals and supplies, the report added.
The truck was raised planeside and positioned at a door on the opposite side of the aircraft’s main entrance.
The reporters, who believed they were traveling with Trump, were instructed to lower their window shades before takeoff. Trump then flew to Mildenhall aboard the C-32A.
The operation came as US forces were conducting large-scale unprovoked attacks on Iran.
The attacks breached both a ceasefire and a subsequent memorandum of understanding, which were meant to halt the cycle of escalation triggered by the American-Israeli aggression launched against Iran on February 28.
As Trump visited Turkey, the Iranian armed forces were delivering a firm retaliatory response to the violations by striking American interests in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News have previously reported that US intelligence officials had raised concerns at the time about a potential operation against Trump or his aircraft.
After arriving at Mildenhall, Trump was photographed disembarking from the presidential aircraft before boarding a new Qatar-provided plane for the remainder of his journey to Washington.

Security officials reportedly moved Trump onto a smaller C-32A military aircraft, which then flew him quietly toward Britain overnight. Meanwhile, journalists and some White House personnel believed Trump remained aboard the larger presidential aircraft throughout the entire journey.
The legacy Air Force One continued toward Britain, effectively serving as a decoy while Trump traveled separately aboard Reach 18. Reports say the operation followed intelligence indicating a credible Iranian threat against Trump or whichever aircraft carried him safely afterward.
The security concern intensified after renewed American strikes against Iran, raising fears about possible attacks targeting the president directly overseas. Officials reportedly considered the newer Qatari-provided Boeing 747-8 less suitable because it lacked some defensive countermeasures available elsewhere currently.
Trump secret flight from Turkey remained unknown publicly until the Washington Post revealed details of the unusual deception operation today. The report says Trump left the 747 through another door before entering a catering truck positioned beside the aircraft nearby.
That vehicle transported him toward the C-32A, allowing security teams to conceal his actual departure from observers nearby on site. The episode highlights extraordinary presidential security concerns and the lengths officials may take when intelligence points toward potential threats today.

sources.news_title: The decoy Air Force One: Details of Trump's secret flight from Turkey
sources.text:
The details of the elaborate ruse that saw US President Donald Trump whisked out of Turkey last month, where he arrived to attend the NATO summit, had him hiding in a food truck before being moved into a military jet. All these were part of the security measures following secret information that the Iranians had plotted a plan to assassinate him.
A report that appeared in the Washington Post said the 80-year-old President boarded the old Air Force One jet in Turkey in front of the media on July 8, but was shortly after secretly transported to a smaller third plane via an airport catering truck.
After Israeli intelligence shared new intelligence with the United States regarding an alleged specific Iranian plot to assassinate President Donald Trump, the President himself announced that he would be leaving Ankara aboard the old Air Force One instead of the luxury 747-8 donated by Qatar that he had flown in on.
He explained it, stating he was making the switch for “old time’s sake.”
Trump was also caught on camera boarding the old Air Force One from the left-side door. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth also boarded the C-32A aircraft via the external stairs in an effort to make the flight seem normal, the outlet reported.
At that time, major media reported that the switch to an older plane was partly driven by concern about the security of the new plane donated by Qatar, which lacked the defensive capabilities of older versions.
However, this act was a decoy. Trump was spirited off that plane via a catering container that had been lifted to the opposite side of the plane. He was then taken to a third plane, which he flew in secret to Britain. The third plane that carried the president to Britain from Turkey was a C-32A, a military variant of a Boeing 757.
The reporters and some White House staff onboard the plane had no idea that Trump was not with them inside the flight. They unwittingly served as decoys.
After the military jet landed in Britain, Trump was secretly moved back to the older version of the Air Force One. He then disembarked in view of reporters and walked across the tarmac to the plane donated by Qatar, which he flew to Washington.
Though the President rarely travels without the reporters for the sake of transparecy, experts believe the agency has long prioritised the security of the president over transparency with the public.
According to Donald Mihalek, a former Secret Service agent who worked in the protective details for George Bush and President Barack Obama, the Secret Service has used decoy motorcades and flights in the past to move presidents secretly. “
“The agency is not the agency of public affairs,” he said. “The agency is the agency of the Secret Service. Their number one job is to keep the president safe. Anytime the president is in a theatre where there’s potential combat danger, the Secret Service has employed protective countermeasures including the use of a decoy,” Mihalek told The New York Post.

sources.news_title: Trump smuggled out of Air Force 1 to military jet in Turkey amid threats: Report
sources.text:
Trump smuggled out of Air Force 1 to military jet in Turkey amid threats: Report
text_fields
New York: US President Donald Trump was hidden in a food truck after boarding Air Force 1 in Turkey and smuggled onto a military aeroplane bound for Britain due to "credible threats" against his official plane, according to sources.
After openly boarding the Air Force 1 in Ankara in front of the media last month, he and some important aides boarded a catering truck lifted to the plane's level, according to The Washington Post on Monday, IANS reported.
He was moved to a car from the food truck, which “had been fitted to the belly of the plane”, and taken to a smaller C32A military jet, The New York Times said.
He and the small group of aides flew to the British Air Force base Mildenhall, where he switched to the Qatari-donated plane for the next leg of the flight to the US, both newspapers reported, quoting unnamed officials.
Meanwhile, the other officials and the reporters, who had boarded Air Force 1, flew on the older plane to Britain and joined Trump on the onward trip, oblivious to Trump having made the switch.
Journalists on the plane reported that they had been asked to keep the windows closed during the flight.
The White House did not confirm or deny the reports about the operation that sounds like a spy thriller, but White House communications director Steven Cheung hinted that the president’s trip faced security issues requiring special measures.
He said, “As the president has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats”.
There was another drama behind the return journey on July 8 from the NATO summit in Ankara.
The plane gifted by Qatar, which Trump flaunted as a showpiece because of its luxuries, was used for Trump’s trip to Ankara.
But the Secret Service and other security officials did not consider that the hasty upgrades it received had given it the level of security of the older Air Force 1s.
Therefore, they first made the switch to an older Air Force 1, and sent the Qatar plane on to Britain, before the switch to the military jet.
Trump said that he had sent the Qatar plane to Britain because US military personnel at the base wanted to see the plane.
However, reports said the reason was the ”credible threats” that had been intercepted, and the Qatar plane’s upgrades did not include the anti-missile defence systems and the wiring to resist electromagnetic surges that the older Air Force 1s had.
It appears that the Secret Service and other security officials later thought that even the older Air Force 1 was not safe enough and decided to smuggle Trump to the military jet, a variant of Boeing 757 without the ostentatious luxuries he is fond of.
When The New York Times exposed the inadequacies of the Qatar-donated plane quoting official sources, the Department of Justice issued subpoenas to the reporters as well as to their relatives, including the mother of one of the journalists, demanding their phones.
Officials defended the unusual subpoenas, claiming they wanted to find the leakers they asserted had endangered national security before dropping them because of the backlash.
The accusations of the leaks only confirmed the security issues with the Qatar plane that Trump and officials had denied.
The plane was taken off service “to be maxed out”, Trump said.
The old Air Force 1s and the Qatar-donated plane that is to serve as another Air Force 1 are all variations of Boeing 747s.

sources.news_title: Trump Took Secret Flight Out of Turkey Due to Islamic Republic Threat, The Washington Post Reports
sources.text:
#Trump, #IslamicRepublic, #Turkey, #SecurityThreat, #TheWashingtonPost
WASHINGTON, Aug 10 (Reuters) – U.S. President Donald Trump departed on a secret military flight from Turkey last month when the White House said he was flying aboard Air Force One, an extraordinary move prompted by an Iranian assassination threat, the Washington Post reported Monday.
Trump had taken the newly renovated Qatari-donated jet to Ankara for the NATO summit but he unexpectedly used an older Air Force One when departing the country, a move that prompted questions about the newer plane’s security.
The trip to NATO was the first international travel for the new plane, whose speedy upgrades triggered questions over its cost and security, and took place as hostilities escalated with Iran, which borders Turkey.
Before departing Ankara, Trump said on Truth Social that he would use an older baby blue Air Force One plane “for old time’s sake” to RAF Mildenhall in Britain while the new plane stopped at the same base so U.S. service members stationed there could tour the aircraft.
After Trump boarded the old Air Force One in front of cameras in Ankara, he was secretly shuttled by an airport catering truck to a smaller plane, an Air Force C-32A, the Post reported citing a U.S. official familiar with the operation and corroborating material it reviewed.
The deception operation was triggered by a credible threat to Trump, the Post reported. A similar operation had taken place in 2000, when President Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as decoy.
On this occasion, the journalists who thought they were traveling with Trump on the older Air Force One, which was effectively used as a decoy, reported being advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post said aside from reporters, some White House staff also believed that the president was on board.
When asked later by reporters why they had to keep their shades shut during the flight, Trump said it was because they were “probably on a dangerous flight.” He went onto say: “But if I go, you go. Right?”
The C-32A carrying Trump flew to Britain and arrived at around 10:20 p.m. while the older Air Force One and media, arriving minutes later, the Post reported. It was not clear, the paper said, how Trump was moved from the C-32A back to the older Air Force One.
Trump’s traveling press pool reported he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10:56 p.m. UK local time.
He gave press a peace sign but didn’t walk over to talk to them. He then spent some time greeting service members before walking to the new, Qatar-donated plane.
When asked for comment on the revelation of a secret flight on a third plane, the White House provided a statement from Communications Director Steve Cheung saying the Qatari-donated jet has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the president and his staff.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” Cheung said. It was the same statement provided to the Post.
The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The new plane, with red, white, dark blue and gold livery chosen by Trump, is a Boeing 747 gifted to the United States by Qatar last year and refitted by defense contractor L3Harris Technologies. It was intended to serve as a temporary placement while Boeing (BA.N) struggled to deliver long-delayed next-generation Air Force One planes.
(Reporting by Humeyra Pamuk and Christian Martinez; Editing by Caitlin Webber)

sources.news_title: Trump used elaborate ruse to fly out of Turkey following summit because of Iran threat - OrissaPOST
sources.text:
Ankara(Turkey): President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post on Monday.
The Post said the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the president as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
There have been questions about the safety of the new Qatari-gifted plane
While Trump was in Turkey, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were traveling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane — suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were traveling with him.
Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional investigation.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Trump said. He added to the traveling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”

sources.news_title: Amid Iranian Assassination Threat, Trump Secretly Flew Out Of Turkiye On C-32A; Air Force One Served As Decoy
sources.text:
Washington DC: Shortly after attending the NATO Summit in Turkiye on July 8, US President Donald Trump took a secret flight out of the country amid threats of an Iranian assassination attempt, according to a report by the Washington Post.
The clandestine mission, which was not reported earlier, was carried out unbeknownst to journalists and some White House staff members who believed they were on the same plane as President Trump, as per the material reviewed by the Washington Post, a US official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the President's travel who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
According to corroborating material reviewed by the Washington Post and the US official, while Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of cameras, he was secretly shuttled out minutes later into a smaller plane- the Air Force C-32A via an airport catering truck used typically to load meals and other supplies pre-flight.
To exit that plane without being seen, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated plane-side using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One's entrance, according to the U.S. official and other corroborating material reviewed by the Washington Post.
Hence, the Air Force One was a "decoy" with media and some members of the White House staff aboard, as per the official.
The blue-and-white C-32A, a modified Boeing 757 used to transport American government officials, had been flown to Turkiye along with the legacy Air Force One and the former Qatari jet to support the president's visit, the US official said.
Defending the jet gifted by Qatar, White House Communications Director Steven Chueng said in a statement responding to a query by the Washington Post-- "The new Air Force One is a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff,"
"As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," it added.
It further mentioned that Secretary of War Pete Hegseth also boarded the C-32 A separately, using external stairs in order to make the flight appear typical.
According to the Washington Post, while no flight tracker data could be found for the C-32 A, videos posted on Youtube showed the former Qatari jet landing which was followed by a C-32A hours later and the legacy Air Force One several minutes later.
It mentioned that while it was not clear how Trump moved from C-32 A to the legacy Air Force One after landing, the Washington Post said referring a media pool report that he exited the Air Force One at 10:56 PM.
Trump was in Ankara to attend the NATO Summit with world leaders in July.
The decoy has raised questions about how much information the US administration has disclosed about the operation since the President's actual location was concealed from several senior US officials and the American public.
The Washington Post noted its in report that the Trump operation highlighted the depth of concerns US security officials had about POTUS leaving Turkiye-- a country that shares border with Iran.
The US official said that a credible threat to Trump involving Iran set the "deception operation" into motion.
There have been other times in the last 30 years when Air Force One served as a decoy for the president because of a serious threat or because he was flying to a dangerous location, another U.S. official said, declining to elaborate.
(Except for the headline, this article has not been edited by FPJ's editorial team and is auto-generated from an agency feed.)

More than 100 killed after strongest quake this century hits western Colombia
The U.S. Geological Survey said the 7.4-magnitude quake struck at a depth of 107 km (66 miles). Colombia’s Geological Service said it was the strongest earthquake recorded in the country in the 21st century.
More than 100 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, toppling buildings, damaging hospitals and infrastructure and trapping people beneath the rubble in the country’s strongest earthquake this century.
The quake struck just days after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in as president, thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis, with memories still fresh of devastating twin earthquakes in neighboring Venezuela in June, Reuters reported.
“The national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed,” he said in a national address around 1 p.m. local time, upon declaring a national state of emergency and giving a death toll of 111. “The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble.”
De La Espriella visited Quibdo, the capital of coastal Choco province, where he promised rent subsidies for those who have lost homes, and then traveled to Cali, western Colombia’s largest city.
Though he had been expected to give an updated national death toll on Monday evening, De La Espriella offered only figures for Valle del Cauca province, where Cali is located, saying 35 people had died there, while 700 had been injured. Some local media have cited a national total of 132 deaths, though the origin of the figure is unclear.
The U.S. Geological Survey said the 7.4-magnitude quake struck at a depth of 107 km (66 miles). Colombia’s Geological Service said it was the strongest earthquake recorded in the country in the 21st century.
As night fell, rescue workers and volunteers with headlamps hurried to find people still trapped under rubble.
Authorities in Cali, Armenia and Manizales announced curfews, with Cali’s mayor saying threats of looting had forced him to deploy police and military personnel to the streets. De La Espriella promised 1,000 additional security personnel for the city.
Cali authorities said the Petronio Alvarez festival, an annual celebration of Pacific music which was due to start on Wednesday, has been postponed.
Video broadcast by Caracol Television showed a group of people pulling a small baby covered in dust from under a pile of rubble. Caracol reported the six-month-old girl and her mother were rescued from under a five-story building in Cali.
Video from Cali also showed rescue workers rappelling people out from the windows of a local hospital.
BUILDINGS CRUMBLE, AIRPORTS CLOSED
In the hard-hit city of Pereira, rescue workers told local television they were in contact with a young boy trapped under a bakery, and crane operators were working to remove badly damaged parts of buildings.
A four-story building crumbled in Pereira during the quake, according to Reuters-verified video, while footage from Manizales showed one of the side towers of the city’s landmark neo-Gothic cathedral collapsing and scattering debris onto nearby streets.
Reuters video showed rescue workers, police and volunteers shoveling debris by hand and loading rubble into trucks as they searched for survivors trapped beneath collapsed buildings. Other footage showed damage to residential towers and emergency-service facilities, with debris crashing onto ambulances parked below.
Mauricio Andrade, a firefighter in Cali, said his team had rescued two adult women and two children from a collapsed building. As he spoke to Reuters, his team was preparing to rescue more people from the rubble.
“They are alive,” he said. “We are making space so we can free them and get them out.”
Carmen Yasmin Garcia, 43, a Cali resident and rescue volunteer, said her group had helped seven people out of a fallen building but there were still four people and a dog trapped underneath.
“A moment ago there was scratching but now we can’t hear anything, we still have faith that the dog is alive and we can get these people out,” she said. “The more people lending a hand the better.”
Saul Paz, 69, a resident of a Cali residential complex that partially collapsed, told Reuters he had been in the dining room with his son and wife when the shaking began.
“I think if it had lasted five seconds more there would be nothing left,” he said. “There are people who went to bed last night with a house and a car and today they won’t have anything.”
Colombia’s civil aviation authority suspended operations at several airports in the region, including Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, while engineers carried out structural inspections.
RING OF FIRE
Colombia sits along the seismically active Pacific Ring of Fire and records thousands of mostly minor earthquakes each month.
Northwestern University seismologist Suzan van der Lee said the quake’s powerful magnitude, inland location and strike-slip motion may have amplified damage in populated valleys despite its considerable depth.
“This one was far below the crust, and in theory it shouldn’t cause as much shaking. At this magnitude, it did actually cause a lot of shaking,” she said, adding Colombia is particularly difficult for seismologists to analyze due to the interaction of several major tectonic plates.
The Colombian Geological Service said it had recorded 21 aftershocks by late Monday and warned that additional tremors were likely.
Colombia’s coffee region was devastated by a magnitude 6.2 earthquake in 1999 that killed more than 1,000 people, particularly around Armenia and Pereira.

sources.news_title: Donald Trump Assassination Threat: Secret Escape From Turkey In Catering Truck Revealed
sources.text:
A startling revelation has surfaced regarding the security protocols of Donald Trump during his recent visit to Ankara, Turkey. Reports indicate that a high-stakes, clandestine operation was executed to protect the former president from a potential assassination plot orchestrated by Iran. According to detailed accounts, Trump was forced to abandon his standard high-profile departure and was instead smuggled to a military airfield inside a clandestine catering truck. This extraordinary measure was taken following credible intelligence regarding threats to his life from Iranian entities, especially given Turkey's shared border with Iran. The Washington Post was the first to break the details of this high-security maneuver that took place during a NATO summit.
The Secret Maneuver in Ankara
The incident occurred during Trump's visit to the Turkish capital for a NATO summit. While the public expected the president to travel in the grandeur of the newly upgraded Boeing 747-8 aircraft—a plane provided by Qatar—security concerns dictated a far more discreet exit. The Washington Post reported that the operation was designed to mislead any potential attackers. A video captured during the event showed a catering truck being lowered from the old Air Force One shortly after Trump had ostensibly boarded it. This truck then moved toward a C-32A aircraft parked at a distance, which was the actual vessel intended for Trump's departure. This operation took place on 8 July, a time when tensions between the United States and Iran were escalating Importantly.

sources.text:
WASHINGTON — In an extraordinary security operation triggered by a credible assassination threat from Iran, U.S. President Donald Trump was secretly shuttled via an airport catering truck to board a military aircraft and leave Turkey following a NATO summit last month, according to reports published Monday by The Washington Post and The New York Times.
The elaborate deception operation took place on July 8 at Ankara International Airport in Turkey. While the White House had publicly announced that the president was departing aboard the primary U.S. presidential aircraft, Trump briefly boarded the U.S. presidential Boeing 747 in full view of television news cameras before being surreptitiously moved into a catering cart (a service vehicle typically used to load meals and inflight supplies) and driven to a smaller, secondary U.S. military plane.
A High-Stakes ‘Deception Operation’
According to U.S. officials familiar with the operation, the complex swap was set in motion due to intelligence indicating a credible safety threat targeting the president from Iranian forces or proxies. Hostilities between Washington and Tehran have escalated sharply in recent months along the Turkish-Iranian border region.
Once inside the catering truck, Trump was driven across the tarmac to an waiting U.S. Air Force C-32A, a military transport variant of the Boeing 757. The primary jumbo jet, along with accompanying White House staff and traveling journalists who believed the president was on board, took off as a high-visibility decoy.
Inflight, reporters aboard the decoy aircraft were instructed by staff to keep all cabin window shades tightly closed. When journalists later questioned Trump about the unusual request, he remarked, “You were probably on a dangerous flight. But if I go, you go. Right?”
Rendezvous in the U.K.
Both aircraft flew in tandem toward RAF Mildenhall in the United Kingdom, arriving within minutes of each other around 10:20 p.m. local time. Trump was subsequently re-transferred onto the primary presidential jet without detection before stepping off the aircraft to greet military personnel and media members waiting on the tarmac.
The tactical decoy operation draws parallels to a similar maneuver in 2000, when President Bill Clinton utilized an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending the standard Air Force One aircraft ahead as a decoy.
In a statement responding to reports of the Ankara incident, White House Communications Director Steve Cheung emphasized that military and security teams utilize robust measures to safeguard the commander-in-chief.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” Cheung said.

sources.news_title: Trump va fugir de Turquia en un avió camuflat, per por a un atac de l'Iran contra l'Air Force One
sources.text:
11.08.2026 - 04:50
|
Actualització: 11.08.2026 - 10:04
The Washington Post · Dan Lamothe, John Hudson, Andrew Ba Tran i Joyce Sohyun Lee
Una amenaça d’assassinat per part de l’Iran contra el president Donald Trump va provocar una operació extraordinària el mes passat en què aquest va volar en secret des de Turquia en una aeronau militar alternativa mentre la Casa Blanca assegurava que viatjava a bord de l’Air Force One, segons que ha sabut The Washington Post.
Aquesta missió clandestina, de la qual no s’havia informat anteriorment, es va dur a terme sense que ho sabessin els periodistes i alguns membres del personal de la Casa Blanca que es pensaven que viatjaven al mateix avió que el president, segons el material revisat per The Post, un funcionari dels Estats Units familiaritzat amb l’operació i una altra persona que en tenia coneixement. Aquestes persones han parlat anònimament perquè no estaven autoritzades a comentar el tema.
El govern americà ha sostingut que Trump va partir de Turquia el 8 de juliol a bord de l’antic Air Force One. Trump va anunciar en xarxes socials que utilitzaria l'”antic Air Force One” en comptes de l’avió que el va portar allà, un nou Boeing 747-8 regalat als Estats Units per Catar i que ell vol fer servir, malgrat les crítiques rebudes sobre la seva seguretat.
A Ànkara, Trump va pujar a l’antic Air Force One a la vista de les càmeres de televisió i els fotògrafs. Però minuts més tard va abandonar l’aparell i va ser traslladat en secret a un avió més petit -un C-32A de la Força Aèria- a través d’un camió de càtering de l’aeroport, dels que normalment es fan servir per a carregar aliments i altres subministraments, segons que ha explicat el funcionari dels EUA i The Post ha contrastat amb material gràfic gravat aquell dia.
Trump havia anat a Ànkara per a una cimera de l’OTAN amb líders mundials. L’operació va ocórrer una nit després que les forces dels EUA renovessin els atacs militars contra l’Iran per ordre de Trump, després del trencament de les negociacions entre Washington i Teheran per posar fi a la guerra.
The Post ha proporcionat a la Casa Blanca els detalls de la seva investigació, juntament amb una llista de preguntes. En resposta, la directora de comunicacions de la Casa Blanca, Steven Cheung, només ha emès una declaració defensant l’avió regalat per Catar. Un portaveu del Pentàgon i un portaveu del Servei Secret no han respost a una sol·licitud de comentari sobre els fets presentada per aquest diari.
Públicament, la Casa Blanca ha repetit el seu relat, segons el qual el president va deixar Turquia a bord del vell Boeing 747 pintat de blau i blanc que va servir com Air Force One abans que Trump comencés a utilitzar l’antic avió regalat per Catar.
Però la realitat no és aquesta, i el que va passar fa palesa com era de gran la preocupació que els responsables de la seguretat del president tenien sobre una amenaça rebuda des de l’Iran. Turquia, un aliat clau dels EUA i membre de l’aliança militar de l’OTAN, comparteix frontera amb l’Iran.
L’amenaça va posar en marxa una “operació d’engany”, segons que explica el funcionari entrevistat pel Washington Post. The New York Times i CBS News ja havien informat el mes passat que els oficials de la intel·ligència havien avisat d’una amenaça específica d’un atac contra el president o el seu avió i que això havia provocat l’adopció de precaucions addicionals. Però no se sabia que havia abandonat l’Air Force One.
Segons el material revisat per The Post i el funcionari dels EUA, nombroses persones van participar en l’engany, algunes sense saber-ho. I els periodistes que es pensaven que viatjaven amb el president a bord de l’Air Force One no van ser notificats mai que aquest havia canviat d’aeronau ni se’ls va fer saber que hi havia una amenaça directa i concreta contra l’avió.
El nou Air Force One regalat per Catar va partir de Turquia primer, a primeres hores de la nit del 8 de juliol. Trump va pujar llavors al vell Air Force One al capvespre, saludant amb la mà cap a la càmera i deixant-se veure, visiblement.
Per sortir d’aquell avió sense ser vist, Trump i diversos ajudants van pujar de seguida en un camió de càtering de l’aeroport, que estava al costat oposat de l’entrada de l’Air Force One.
Les fotografies i imatges preses pels mitjans de comunicació a l’aeroport turc mostren efectivament l’escala a un costat de l’Air Force One, per on va pujar Trump, i el camió de càtering aparcat a l’altra banda de l’aparell, amb el seu contenidor elevat al nivell de l’avió.
Trump va arribar en una limusina, va pujar per l’escala i va saludar cap a la pista. Pocs minuts més tard, mentre els membres del cos de premsa de la Casa Blanca pujaven per la part de darrere de l’avió, un home amb americana va entrar en la cabina del camió de càtering, segons s’ha pogut comprovar amb les imatges gravades. Aleshores el contenidor va ser abaixat i el vehicle es va allunyar de l’Air Force One en direcció a un avió C-32A més petit, que era a prop i sense despertar sospites.
Aquest avió C-32A blau i blanc és un Boeing 757 modificat utilitzat per transportar funcionaris del govern dels EUA, que havia volat a Turquia juntament amb l’Air Force One i l’antic avió de Catar. Porta també ben visibles les paraules “United States of America” i pot ser utilitzat per transportar el president o el vicepresident.
El secretari de defensa Pete Hegseth va pujar aquest avió a la vista de tothom, en el que sembla un intent de fer veure que aquell era un vol normal. Hegseth va volar, però, amb Trump en l’avió petit, sense que gairebé ningú ho sabés. Mentrestant els periodistes que pujaven a l’Air Force One, van trobar-se que el personal de la Casa Blanca els indicava que havien de tancar les persianes de les finestres, per motius de seguretat.
L’expressió Air Force One en realitat no defineix l’avió. Qualsevol avió on vola el president s’identifica davant els controladors com “Air Force One”. En aquesta ocasió, però, l’engany va continuar perquè el vol del C-32A va fer servir l’identificador “Reach 18” o “RCH18”, segons una persona familiaritzada amb la missió i altre material revisat per The Post.
El compte d’aviació “Thenewarea51” va notificar l’arribada a la Gran Bretanya del C-32A que transportava Trump en secret i va informar que els sistemes que permeten que l’aeronau sigui fàcilment rastrejada mentre està en l’aire havien estat apagats. Els indicadors Reach sovint s’utilitzen per als vols de transport de personal i els que transporten equipament militar, segons persones familiaritzades amb la missió.
Les dades públiques de seguiment de vols mostren que l’Air Force One regalat per Catar va volar a la base aèria de Mildenhall (Regne Unit) fent servir l’identificador “SAM 33”, una abreviació comuna per a “special air mission”. Va aterrar a Mildenhall a les 6:26 pm hora local el 8 de juliol.
L’Air Force One antic, que portava el personal de la Casa Blanca i els periodistes va aparèixer en el radar prop d’Istambul de camí cap al Regne Units, inicialment sense identificador. Però, poc després, malgrat que el president no estava a bord, va fer servir l’identificador Air Force One, “AF1”. Va arribar a Mildenhall al voltant de les 10:29 pm hora local.
No s’han pogut trobar dades del vol del C-32A on viatjava clandestinament el president Trump, però els vídeos publicats pels comptes de YouTube RankUpAviation i Military Aviation Channel mostren l’avió regalat per Catar aterrant, seguit per un C-32A unes hores més tard, al voltant de les 10:20 pm, i l’Air Force One diversos minuts més tard.
Els vídeos d’afeccionats en YouTube no mostren Trump en cap moment, ni sortint del C-32A ni entrant a l’Air Force One, ja que els avions van aparcar en una àrea remota de l’aeroport.
No és clar com Trump va tornar des del C-32A a l’Air Force One després d’aterrar, però el fet és que el president va aparèixer davant de les càmeres de televisió i va baixar per les escales de l’Air Force One al voltant de les 10:56 pm, com si hi hagués viatjat.
Després de saludar diverses persones, el president va embarcar en el nou Air Force One, el que li ha regalat Catar, per viatjar de tornada a Washington, amb personal i premsa a bord al voltant de les 11:01 pm. A bord del nou Air Force One, Trump va parlar als periodistes durant uns 15 minuts, destacant l’amenaça que l’Iran representa però sense reconèixer res del que havia passat d’ençà que havia sortit d’Ànkara.
Quan se li va preguntar per què el personal de l’avió havia demanat als periodistes que baixessin les persianes de les finestres a la sortida de Turquia, Trump va dir que era “perquè probablement anàveu en un vol perillós per culpa dels malvats amb els quals hem de tractar.” Trump va afegir que ell està “amenaçat tot el temps” i que és el “número u” en la “llista” de l’Iran.
“Però si jo vaig en l’avió, vosaltres aneu també. Oi?” va afegir el president sense donar cap pista respecte al fet que ell no hi anava. “Potser algun dia voldreu canviar de professió”, va afegir.

sources.text:
US officials secretly moved President Trump onto a different aircraft as he left Turkey last month, after identifying what they considered a credible assassination threat from Iran, The Washington Post has reported. The operation kept the press pool and some White House staff in the dark, who believed they were on the same plane as the president the entire time.
The switch took place July 8, one night after US forces resumed strikes on Iran following the collapse of ceasefire talks, as Trump departed Ankara after a NATO leaders summit. He had arrived in Turkey aboard the newly retrofitted Boeing 747-8 that Qatar gave the US — the plane’s first international trip carrying a president. Trump said at the time he’d fly home on the older Air Force One instead, so US troops stationed in Britain could see the new jet. That wasn’t the real reason.
The Qatari jet left Turkey first that evening for RAF Mildenhall in Britain. Trump then boarded an older Air Force One in Ankara in full view of cameras. Minutes later, he and several aides slipped through a door on the opposite side of the plane into an airport catering truck, out of sight of anyone not involved in the operation. The truck lowered him to the ground and drove him to a third aircraft — a modified Boeing 757 known as the C-32A, typically used for senior officials but also cleared to carry the president or vice president.
Trump flew to Britain aboard the C-32A, landing at around 10:20 p.m. The decoy Air Force One, carrying the press pool, touched down roughly nine minutes later. Staff had told reporters aboard to lower their window shades before takeoff in Ankara. How Trump got from the C-32A back onto the older Air Force One isn’t clear, but by around 11 p.m. he was back in front of cameras, descending its stairs, greeting US service members and boarding the Qatari-gifted jet for the flight home to Washington.
The White House has kept saying Trump flew home from Turkey on the older Air Force One, posting a photo of that aircraft the night he landed in Britain. When the Post put its findings to the administration, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung defended the new jet’s security rather than address the deception, calling it, “a state-of-the-art aircraft equipped with high-level security protocols.”

sources.news_title: Trump used elaborate ruse to fly out of Turkey following summit because of Iran threat, report says - Now Georgia
sources.text:
President Donald Trump secretly flew out of last month’s NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, on an alternate military aircraft while the White House made it appear that the Republican president was flying on Air Force One, according to a report published by The Washington Post on Monday.
The Post said the operation was prompted by an Iranian assassination threat against Trump. The ruse was carried out as journalists and some White House staff members were led to believe they were on the same plane as the president as he began his journey back to Washington from the annual gathering of NATO country leaders.
The Post cited material reviewed by the newspaper, a U.S. official familiar with the operation and another person with knowledge of the president’s travel. The Associated Press has not independently confirmed the report.
Trump had flown to the summit in a new Qatari-gifted and retrofitted red, white and navy blue jet. But ahead of departing Turkey, he said he would fly partway home on an older-model baby blue Air Force One plane instead.
The president at the time said the new luxury jet was being flown out ahead of his departure from Ankara to give some U.S. troops based in eastern England a chance to check out the new Air Force One.
In Ankara, Trump boarded the old Air Force One jumbo jet in view of television cameras ahead of the plane flying to Royal Air Force Mildenhall in the United Kingdom.
However, according to the Post report, after boarding the legacy Air Force One jet, he was secretly shuttled minutes later to a smaller plane — an Air Force C-32A — via an airport catering truck typically used to load meals and other supplies. Trump flew to Mildenhall on that smaller jet.
The White House did not respond directly to questions about the Post report of the secret operation to whisk Trump out of the country on a third aircraft, or the reported elaborate ruse to make it appear he was on the baby blue Air Force One jet flying to Mildenhall.
“As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement.
The U.S. Secret Service declined to comment. The Air Force, which maintains the fleet of executive travel aircraft, referred questions to the White House.
There have been questions about the safety of the new Qatari-gifted plane
While Trump was in Turkey, the U.S. military conducted a series of large strikes in Iran in retaliation for its attacks on merchant shipping in the region.
The New York Times and CBS News reported last month that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a potential attack on the president or his jet, triggering additional precautions and the decision not to use the newly inaugurated aircraft gifted to Trump by Qatar for the first leg of Trump’s trip home from Ankara.
The swap had spurred questions about the security of the Qatar-provided aircraft, and Trump said last month after the trip that it would undergo additional upgrades.
Cheung on Monday maintained that the new, Qatari-gifted plane was “a state-of-the-art aircraft that has been fitted with high-level security protocols that ensure the safety of the President and his staff.”
The new Post report on clandestinely putting Trump on a third aircraft and quietly whisking him out of the country adds a fresh layer to just how seriously concerned U.S. security officials were about the threat against Trump during the ongoing war with Iran.
Paul Eckloff, a former special agent with the Secret Service, said such an unusual move could either reflect actionable intelligence or an abundance of caution given volatility in the region with the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
“I would not say unprecedented, but it is an unusual occurrence,” Eckloff told The Associated Press.
The Post reported that to exit that plane without being seen by those uninvolved in the operation, Trump and several aides stepped aboard an airport catering truck, which was elevated planeside using hydraulics and positioned at a door on the opposite side of Air Force One’s entrance.
The small group of reporters who thought they were traveling with Trump were advised to lower their window shades ahead of takeoff.
After arriving at Mildenhall, news photographers captured images of Trump getting off the presidential plane — suggesting he reboarded Air Force One out of sight of the pack of journalists who thought they were traveling with him.
Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal called for a congressional investigation.
“It is unprecedented and it is surreal,” he said Monday on CNN, calling the incident “downright scary.”
After the brief visit to the base at Mildenhall, Trump boarded the new Air Force One aircraft to fly the rest of the way to Washington.
During a gaggle with reporters aboard the aircraft, Trump was asked directly if there was any credible threats on Air Force One by Iran.
“Well, I have a threat all the time. I’m number one on their list before you,” Trump said. He added to the traveling reporters, “But if I go, you go.”
